items.title: [Roadmap]: SGLang Distributed KVCache System For Agentic Workload
items.body:
### Motivation

As agentic workloads drive rapid growth in KV cache storage and transfer volumes, the existing PD disaggregation + HiCache stack is hitting significant bottlenecks. Meanwhile, HiCache's compatibility with hybrid models and other evolving features remains limited. There is an urgent need for a robust, high-performance distributed KV cache system capable of sustaining the heavy demands of large-scale agentic scenarios.

The core objective is to achieve end-to-end integration of PD incremental transfer, HiCache / HiSparse, pipeline parallelism, and Eagle — validated at scale on DeepSeek DSA (V32、GLM5) and Linear model (Qwen35) families.

### Q3 Roadmap

- [ ] **Agentic KV Cache Scheduling**
  - [x] Support session-aware RadixTree and HiCache ([PR #29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173))
  - [ ] Build a KV cache orchestrator across the router and engine to detect agentic workflows—including sessions, sub-agents, and tool calls—and provide scheduling hints such as `PREFETCH`, `DEMOTE`, and `PIN`; integrate with the router roadmap for global KV cache scheduling ([Issue #25760](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760)) @hzh0425 
  - [x] Support direct L3 cache mode to enable a larger globally shared memory pool https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35687 @hzh0425 @huangtingwei9988 @maning00 
  - [ ] Enable supernode-wide sharing of L1 and L3 KV caches through Router scheduling and linker mode.
  - [x] Build a CPU-only KV cache simulator that replays representative agentic workloads without GPUs ([Issue #21891](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21891)) @littlefatfat
  - [ ] Support KVCache Sequence Split Mode to distribute VRAM pressure evenly. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30501 @Shunkangz 
    - [x] [PR #38356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38356) — Add logical-page placement and a rotated allocator to distribute KV pages evenly across shard ranks.
    - [x] [PR #37615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37615) — Add sharded KV pools that store each rank's owned pages and assemble the full prefix for prefill attention.
    - [x] [PR #38468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38468) — Add the KV cache sharding flag and wire the sharded pools into prefill scheduling and capacity checks.
  - [ ] Support Unified-KVCache Layout https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33651 @Shunkangz  @huangtingwei9988 
    - [ ] [PR #39727](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39727) — Add the page-unified host KV layout and topology-independent L3 keys for KV chunks.
    - [x] [PR #39726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39726) — Add a JIT kernel that loads page-unified host KV back to the device one layer at a time.
    - [ ] [PR #39815](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39815) — Connect page-unified host pools and unified storage keys to the HiCache linker path.
 
- [ ] **UnifiedRadixTree Enhancements**
  - [x] Decouple the tree core and implement it in Rust to accelerate hot paths such as matching and eviction ([PR #29901](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29901)) 、https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32710
  - [ ] Integrate with KVCache-Canary to enable debugging capabilities for KV cache correctness. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32476

- [ ] **PD Disaggregation Integration**
  - [ ] Support an L2 `DecodeRadixTree` to increase transfer batch sizes and reduce GPU memory usage
  - [ ] Support SWA/DsV4/Mamba/DSpark with decode unified radix treee
  - [ ] Explore a proof of concept for Prefill-as-a-Service

- [ ] **HiSparse Production Readiness**
  - [ ] Improve the reliability and production readiness of HiSparse ([Issue #28874](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28874))


### Q2 Roadmap
The roadmap below is still incomplete and will be expanded with more content related to Agent/SubAgent KVCache.

- [x] **HiCache: Support Hybrid Model** (Linear & DSA)   @hzh0425 
  - [x] Hybrid Cache Controller & Support Linear Hybrid Model https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20457
  - [x] Mooncake backend support for hybrid model https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21259 @huangtingwei9988 
  - [ ] Support MLA + Mamba Hybrid model(KeLing) https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22957
  - [x] 3FS Backend support for hybrid model https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23241 @kangyifei
  - [x] HiCache support for Unified Hybrid Radix Cache https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/20415
  - [x] Support DeepSeekV4 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24691
  - [x] Support MiMO-V2 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27378
  - [ ] Dedup MLA KV cache in host memory across TP ranks https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26691

- [ ] **PD-Decode Support HiCache**  @hzh0425 @huangtingwei9988 
  - [x] Support Decode Side RadixTree @ishandhanani 
  - [ ] Support Decode Side HybridRadixTree (SWA/Mamba) (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27770)
  - [x] Storage Prefetch Interface — Expose a prefetch API that allows newly arriving decode requests to query storage hits and initiate Storage→Host→Device prefetch directly
  - [ ] Support L2 RadixTree to increase cache hit rate
  - [ ] Storage supports the concept of groups, enabling unified visibility and eviction for groups composed of multiple keys within a page (e.g., key and value, split by rank, etc.). @huangtingwei9988 
  - [ ] Heterogeneous TP Support For PD With HiCache @huangtingwei9988 

- [x] **PD Disaggregation**：Idea provided by @ShangmingCai  @hzh0425 
  - [x] **Incremental KV Transfer** — Decode queries storage for cached prefix tokens and reports the hit count to Prefill via protocol extension; Prefill only transfers the non-cached (incremental) portion
  - [x] **PD Host TransferMode** — Prefill transfers the KV cache directly to Decode's DRAM, bypassing the GPU as an intermediary；Helps increase the decode-side batch size in long-context scenarios. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21591
  - [ ] **Support for large decode batches:** During decoding, use the L2 and L3 prefix portions cached on the host (hit from prior computations) along with the incremental part transferred from the prefill phase; then load everything back onto the GPU to perform subsequent inference steps.

- [x] **Agent/Rollout KVCache Management** @hzh0425 @stmatengss @ishandhanani 
  - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24656
  - [x] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574

- [x] **HiCache Compatibility with Other Features**
  - [x] PP × HiCache Consistency Fix — Resolve compatibility issues between PP and HiCache by synchronizing Rank 0's cache events across PP ranks via event numbering, ensuring RadixTree state consistency @hzh0425  @whybeyoung https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22607
  - [x] MTP  × HiCache https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21125 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30393
  - [x] EP & DP   × HiCache
  - [x] CP  × HiCache   https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20460
  - [x] Support CP Layer-Wise Split With HiCache: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29421


### Related resources

_No response_

items.title: [Agentic Inference] Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic Workloads
items.body:
# RFC: Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic Workloads

Authors: @ishandhanani, @hzh0425

## Introduction 

> [!NOTE]  
> Note: For this RFC, we will define “router” as an orchestrator on top of multiple engine units. 

Agent workloads make the value of a KV block predictable from above the engine, but that value is invisible to request-local LRU. We propose exposing a narrow, router-initiated hint surface so an external router can pass cache intent to SGLang without making invasive changes to the engine scheduler and cache manager. In this way, SGLang keeps ownership of scheduling and memory and is free to clip, defer, or reject any hint. 

Today the engine can identify cached content and local residency, but it does not know why a trajectory will reuse a prefix or how long an external tool/subagent gap will last. Session membership is useful metadata for lifecycle-scoped policies, but it is not the only way to address KV: request-scoped hints can name an exact token prefix after tokenization.

The session work in [#27058](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27058) remains complementary. It lets the engine associate radix ownership with a session when the policy is genuinely session-scoped. The first L3 Pin POC described below is deliberately token-relative and does not require session identity.

With the work that is being done in PRs like 
1. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20535 - allow for HiCache to become buffer mode and allow L3 cache to take more space on nodes. Buffer-mode isn't strictly required but the idea of giving L3 more memory is useful here
2. https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2214 - allow for MC to start sending KV events which indexers can use

We can leverage L3 cache as the shared retention and movement substrate. The router expresses intent; SGLang resolves that intent against exact radix content and remains responsible for allocation, transfer completion, and visibility; the storage backend owns stored-object lifecycle.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["Router / orchestrator policy"] --> K["Provider-neutral KV hint"]
    K --> S["SGLang scheduler + HiCache"]
    S <--> G["L1: GPU KV"]
    S <--> H["L2: host KV"]
    S <--> M["L3: shared storage / Mooncake"]
    M -. retain now; share, prefetch, demote later .-> S
```

The hint surface is broader than any one backend operation. The concrete work so far validates one mapping—bounded Pin intent to a Mooncake L3 lease—without making that mechanism the whole RFC.

## High level roadmap (subject to change)

#### Phase 1 - session based kv cache
1. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29436 - enable a top level `session_id` so that we do not have to hijack `session_params.session_id` which is used for the `StreamingSession` cache
2. https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27058 -  enable `session_id` to be tagged into kv blocks allowing us to refer to kv at the session level
3. TODO - enable `SessionRadixCache` to be implemented at the HiCache layer

#### Phase 2 - design router initiated hint API
1. POC implemented / PRs in progress - carry a provider-neutral `KvHintEnvelope` from an external orchestrator through request preprocessing and into the SGLang engine
2. POC implemented / PRs in progress - map bounded Pin intent onto exact committed HiCache page groups and a Mooncake L3 TTL lease
3. TODO - productionize admission, telemetry, expiry, namespace, and version-skew behavior for L3 Pin
4. TODO - measure request-time L3 restoration before adding proactive Prefetch or Demote execution APIs

## Problem Statement

The orchestrator knows the structure request-local policy cannot: which sessions are live, which token ranges are shared prefixes vs unique tails, which tool gap is 10ms vs 10min, when a subagent opened and closed. The engine sees a block hash and a refcount.

Current shape:

```text
request arrives
  -> router chooses target worker via KV overlap/load
  -> target worker checks local cache
       hit:  reuse
       miss: recompute or apply local offload policy
```

This is insufficient when: 
- another worker already holds the prefix; 
- the workload knows a request will resume soon; 
- a session has ended and its KV should be demoted/freed; 
- the orchestrator wants to protect high-value KV; 
- or local policy cannot tell a short tool gap from a long one.


The missing abstraction is a precise, observable surface where the orchestrator biases the cache manager without owning scheduler or memory internals. Letting an external system manipulate cache internals directly is the wrong design: it is brittle, it duplicates scheduler policy outside the engine, and it forces a refactor of the scheduler/cache-manager boundary. Hints keep ownership inside SGLang and let the orchestrator soft-influence behavior at request and lifecycle boundaries.

---

## Design Principles

1. **Orchestrator owns policy; engine executes.** The agent-graph / workflow intelligence lives outside. The engine understands priority, TTL, session membership, tier - nothing about why. Keeps things simple
2. **Zero overhead when unused.**  Un-hinted workloads behave exactly like today.
3. **Hints are soft, bounded, and safe to reject.** The engine may accept, clip, defer, or ignore. Every hint is observable. Nothing a client says can pin memory unboundedly or deadlock the scheduler.
4. **Router-initiated by default.** Workloads can still emit intent, but the router is where workload context merges with global KV placement, worker load, health, and admission. In production environments, the router has: a global KV index from events, built-in HA/fault-tolerance, existing overlap/load routing + admission control, and (with the harness<->orchestrator work) trajectory awareness, not just request awareness.

---

## Hint Taxonomy (conceptual)

### Share

Reuse a prefix that already lives on another worker or a shared tier: route a continuation to a less-loaded worker but pull the prefix from the old one; share a common prefix across sibling subagents; warm a scale-up worker. It is the existence proof for the whole model: the machinery to move KV natively between workers is what every other hint also needs. We can leverage L3 cache for this. 

### Prefetch

Move KV into a hotter tier *before* it is needed: warm GPU for a likely next-turn prefix; pull shared KV into a freshly selected worker; reload main-agent KV during a subagent's close. This is easily enabled after we get the APIs that the `Share` hint gives us.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Router
    participant W as Worker
    participant L as Mooncake / L3
    participant H as HiCache host / L2
    participant G as GPU / L1
    R->>W: prefetch hint (exact prefix likely needed soon)
    W->>L: locate committed KV in shared L3
    L-->>H: stage KV into worker host cache
    H-->>G: promote only after transfer completion
    Note over W,G: SGLang owns allocation and radix visibility
    R->>W: continuation request arrives
    W->>G: cache hit, skip prefill
    W-->>R: tokens
```

### Demote 

Move KV to a colder tier instead of dropping it: long external tool call, paused trajectory, low-priority-but-reusable subagent state, memory pressure where recompute is expensive. Demote moves together with Prefetch/Onboard - the KV offloaded during a pause is the KV warmed back before the continuation resumes. This is easily enabled after we get the APIs that the `Share` hint gives us.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as Router
    participant W as Worker
    participant G as GPU / L1
    participant H as HiCache host / L2
    participant L as Mooncake / L3
    R->>W: demote hint (long tool gap, pause)
    W->>H: ensure the exact prefix is staged
    H->>L: ensure the prefix is published to shared L3
    Note over W,L: Publication and local reclamation are separate operations
    W->>G: allow local pages to become normally evictable
    R->>W: continuation resumes (paired prefetch)
    L-->>H: restore retained KV
    H-->>G: promote after completion
    W-->>R: tokens
```

### Pin

Keep a high-value prefix protected from ordinary eviction for a **bounded** TTL. Examples include expensive retrieved context, shared planner state, and tool/subagent gaps where recomputation dominates latency. A Pin hint should not imply permanent HBM residency: the engine may realize it at a colder tier while keeping L1/L2 normally evictable.

The first implementation POC realizes Pin at Mooncake L3:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client / agent harness
    participant R as Dynamo router
    participant S as SGLang + HiCache
    participant M as Mooncake L3
    C->>R: OpenAI prompt_cache_retention or Anthropic cache_control
    R->>S: Request + normalized prefix_tokens / ttl_seconds
    S->>S: Resolve exact committed, page-aligned prefix
    S->>M: Queue retain_groups(group_ids, ttl_ms)
    M->>M: Extend current members and future-member deadline
    Note over S,M: GPU and host copies remain normally evictable
    C->>R: Later continuation
    R->>S: Route normally
    S->>M: Existing request-time HiCache L3 lookup
    M-->>S: Retained KV pages
```

- [Mooncake#2835](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2835) adds TTL-bounded `retain_groups`, automatic expiry, future-member inheritance, and bounded group admission.
- Dynamo normalizes provider-native controls into a small `KvHintEnvelope`; SGLang resolves token offsets to exact HiCache page groups and queues the Mooncake metadata operation on its existing storage worker.
- A fresh MiniMax M2.7 H100 A/B evicted 24.18 GB / 95,232 keys under pressure. The unretained cold-worker probe recomputed 10,032 tokens; the one-hour retained probe restored 10,016 tokens from L3 and computed 16.
- This is "low hanging fruit" and can be used to implement Anthropic's `cache_control` API and OpenAI's `prompt_cache` APIs

The implementation uses “retention” because that is the provider API language. In this taxonomy it is a bounded L3 Pin. The Retain concept below remains priority-biased eviction rather than guaranteed lease protection.

### Retain

Bias eviction order rather than protect a prefix with a lease: some token ranges are worth more than others when eviction is unavoidable. The orchestrator attaches a relative priority (optionally with a duration) to a token range, and under memory pressure the engine evicts low-priority KV first. We have existing mechanisms to do this with the `priority` radix-cache strategy and can augment them with duration semantics similar to TensorRT-LLM's `TokenRetentionConfig`.

---

## Non-Goals

- Not a public user-facing cache API; the producer is the router/orchestrator.
- Not direct orchestrator manipulation of cache-manager internals; hints only bias.
- Not a replacement for local prefix matching or for sglang's LRU - it augments and reorders them.
- Not a guarantee the engine obeys any hint; accept/clip/defer/reject is always allowed.
- Not a commitment to freeze the current POC schema. `KvHintEnvelope { retention: [{prefix_tokens, ttl_seconds}] }` is the first exercised shape, not the final taxonomy.

---

## Relationship to existing SGLang work

This RFC is complementary to two in-flight SGLang efforts; it attacks the same agentic-KV problem from a different angle (a router above many engines) rather than from inside a single engine.

- **[#24656](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24656) - Agent-Aware KV Cache (Phase 1)** is the *in-engine, client-driven* angle: an optional `agent_hints` field on the OpenAI request flows into one engine, annotates radix nodes, and feeds an experimental `agent_aware` eviction policy. This RFC is the *router-initiated, multi-engine* angle on the same intent, and the two compose: #24656's `agent_hints` is the natural request-scoped envelope, and its `cache_ttl_ms` / `reuse_hint` are exactly our Pin / Retain hints. This RFC then adds the out-of-band control path and the cross-worker KV *movement* (Share / Prefetch / Demote) that #24656 explicitly defers (HiCache/storage metadata inheritance, cross-process coordination).
- **[#21846](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21846) - Distributed KVCache System for Agentic Workload** is the *mechanism / substrate*: HiCache tiering, PD incremental transfer, a storage prefetch interface, and hybrid-model support. This RFC is the *policy layer* that rides those rails - Share uses the worker-to-worker HiCache movement, Prefetch maps onto the roadmap's storage-prefetch interface, and Demote onto multi-tier offload. #21846 builds the plumbing; the router decides when to use it. Its own "Agent/Rollout KVCache Management" item already points back to #24656, so all three are one arc.

---

## References

<details>
<summary>External RFCs / APIs, research, and our prior work</summary>

External RFCs / APIs:
- vLLM #37003 - Context-Aware KV-Cache Retention API (Prioritized Evictions): (impl PR #38514)
- vLLM #37168 - Active Coordination and Two-Zone Scheduling for Long-Running Agents: (impl vllm-ascend#6722)
- vLLM agentic-api # 18 - Session-aware KV cache management
- vLLM #39305 - Selective KV Cache offload: (impl PR #39983)
- vLLM #38260 - Multi-tier KV offloading via the offloading connector
- TensorRT-LLM `KvCacheRetentionConfig` / `TokenRangeRetentionConfig` (token_start/token_end/priority 0-100/duration_ms; default 35; decode_retention_priority; secondaryOffloadMinPriority)

Research:
- KVCache in the Wild (Alibaba traces): https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02634
- Continuum (KV cache TTL for multi-turn agents): https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02230
- Tail-Optimized Caching for LLM Inference: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15152
- KVFlow (workflow-aware prefix caching): https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07400
- MARCONI (prefix caching for hybrid LLMs): https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19379

Our prior work (sglang / Mooncake):
- #24656 (agent-aware KV phase 1 / API feedback), #21846 (distributed KV roadmap), #27058 (radix-native sessions), #27024 / #27025 (streaming-session deadlock + bound), #22273 / #21875 (streaming-session leak fixes), #18941 (TTL prefix pinning), #21045 (priority retention duration), [Mooncake#2214](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2214) (group semantics), [Mooncake#2835](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2835) (TTL-bounded group retention POC).

Our prior work (dynamo):
- [#7665](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/7665) / [#7377](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/7377) / [#7384](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/7384) (session_control + ephemeral KV routing), pi-dynamo-provider#4 (per-subagent sessions), [#6213](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/6213) / [#6571](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/6571) (Anthropic-style cache_control), [#8789](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/8789) / [#9140](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/9140) (agent_context / ATIF), [#9448](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/9448) (thunderagent_router program scheduler).

</details>

items.title: Agentic Cache Scheduling System Roadmap (Q4)
items.body:
## 1. Agentic Cache Scheduling

- Supernode-wide KV Cache Sharing @hzh0425  @Shunkangz @zhengd-nv 
	- Enable sharing of GPU-resident (L1) and host-resident (L2) KV caches across engines within the same super-node domain.
	- Add cache location awareness to the Router to coordinate request placement and KV transfers based on cache availability and engine load.
	- Extend HiCache linker integration to support GPU-to-GPU KV transfers over (NVLink @Shunkangz、AMD UALoE @TianDi101、SAIL's card-to-card interconnect @Vinsmoke86) and remote Grace DRAM access through EGM.
	- Optimize small KV-page transfers and NUMA placement; validate correctness, cache hit rate, and TTFT/TPOT on GB NVLink72、 AMD MI455X Helios Rack、and SAIL clusters.
- Build a KV cache orchestrator across the router and engine @ZhaiFeiyue @stmatengss 
	- Identify sessions, sub-agents, and tool calls, and expose `PREFETCH`, `DEMOTE`, and `PIN` hints for global cache scheduling. Align this work with the [[router roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760). 
	- Add session-aware scheduling to the router
- Enhance HiCache Linker Mode @hzh0425 @alphabetc1 @huangtingwei9988 
    - [[PR #40896](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40896)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40896): Support fast failover and recovery.
    - [[PR #41343](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41343)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41343): Extend support to hybrid models with Mamba and SWA.
    - [PR #44526](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44526): Support runtime attach and detach of the unified cache external linker through the HiCache storage-backend API.
    - [PR #43831](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43831): Skip redundant write-through of KV pages just loaded by the external linker to reduce storage existence queries and offload overhead.
    - [PR #44623](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44623): Support DeepSeek-V4.1 external linker pools with shared C1/C2 KV and indexer mappings, SWA storage, and packed draft mappings in UMBP.
    - [PR #44977](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44977): Support FULL + MAMBA MLA models such as Kimi-K3 in the direct external linker, including DSPARK sidecar draft KV.
    - Improve reliability and observability for production deployment.
    - Refactor `hybrid_pool_assembler.py`：Simplify pool assembly and improve extensibility across model architectures.
- Support a [[unified KV cache layout](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33651)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33651) for host cache and L3 storage: @Shunkangz @huangtingwei9988 
    - [[PR #39727](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39727)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39727): Add a page-unified host KV layout and topology-independent L3 keys.
    - [[PR #39726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39726)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39726): Add a JIT kernel to load page-unified host KV back to the device one layer at a time.
    - [PR #39728](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39728): Integrate the page-unified layout end to end in HiCache, including GPU-host transfers and topology-independent L3 keys, with initial file-backend support and round-trip tests.
    - [[PR #39815](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39815)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39815): Integrate page-unified host pools and storage keys with the HiCache linker.
    - Add E2E Test For PD + PP/TP + UnifiedLayout @huangtingwei9988 

## 2. Decode Prefix Cache @jojoakm @HZY-Wade 

- Refactor the decode-side HiCache mixin to support L1-only, L1+L2, and L2-only cache configurations.
- Support an L2-only `DecodeRadixTree` to increase KV transfer batch sizes and reduce GPU memory pressure ([[PR #38292](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38292)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38292)).
- [PR #43548](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43548): Limit the L3 prefix advertised to prefill to the span accepted by decode-side prefetch, preventing restore failures when prefetch is declined.
- Extend the decode-side unified radix tree to fully support SWA, Mamba, and MTP.

## 3. Unified KV Cache Sharding for CP @Shunkangz @HZY-Wade 

- [[PR #38356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38356)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38356): Add logical-page placement and a rotated allocator to distribute KV pages across shard ranks.
- [[PR #37615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37615)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37615): Add sharded KV pools that store each rank’s owned pages and assemble the full prefix for prefill attention.
- [[PR #38468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38468)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38468): Wire KV cache sharding into prefill scheduling and capacity checks.
- [PR #38473](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38473): Support P/D transfer for sharded KV caches and add E2E tests for MLA and GQA.
- [PR #44029](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44029): Add zero-SM KV cache all-gather using NCCL copy engines to reduce SM contention with attention and GEMMs.
- TODO: Optimize CPU Overhead and communication
- PR #42973: Extend CP KV cache sharding to GLM DSA and MTP, with P/D transfer and CPU HiCache support for both KV and indexer caches. @HZY-Wade 
- PR #43057: Fuse DSA indexer quantization with scratch/local writes and reuse raw FP8 latent staging, preserving fallbacks for unsupported layouts.  @HZY-Wade 
- Support unified kvcache layout for dcp.
   - TODO: Optimize FlashInfer Kernel

## 4. HiSparse @alphabetc1   @bingps  @Shunkangz 

- Develop HiSparse V2 to coordinate GPU and host memory as a larger decode cache, targeting up to **2× KV capacity** in GB deployments.
- Refactor HiSparse to support more sparse attention model variants through a common architecture.
- Optimize the HiSparse swap-in kernel by overlapping KV prefetch with computation to reduce the performance impact of cache I/O.
- Integrate with TBO, h2d overlap moe

## 5. **Unified Engram Storage** @hzh0425 @stmatengss

- Unify DeepSeek Engram, Qwen PLE, and LongCat N-gram table storage and lookup under `mem_cache`, supporting GPU, host-memory, and file-backed storage.
- Support Mooncake local/remote backends and cross-node sharing of packed FP8 tables ([#4083](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4083)). @magicYang1573
- Reduce remote lookup overhead with metadata snapshots and optimized RDMA scatter ([#4095](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4095), [#4117](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4117)). @zxpdemonio
- Add adaptive scatter/gather in Store `get_into_ranges`, overlapping CPU packing with RDMA transfers ([#4502](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/4502)). @magicYang1573
- Integrate CUDA Graph-compatible asynchronous prefetch into SGLang; validate correctness, memory savings, TTFT, prefill throughput, and decode TPOT. @magicYang1573 @zxpdemonio

## 6. SGLang Simulator @littlefatfat

- Time Predictors
    - [PR #44253](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44253): Migrate NVIDIA time prediction from AIConfigurator to AISimulate.
    - [PR #44299](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44299): Provide baseline data collection and training scripts for ML time predictors.
    - AMD: Integrate InferCast.

    - Support multi-instance simulation for distributed cache scheduling and P/D disaggregation.

    - Model global network latency and bandwidth contention across KV transfers, cache prefetching, and shared-cache access.

items.title: [RFC] First-Class, Versioned KV Hint Envelope for SGLang
items.body:
## Motivation

[#27574](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574) proposes programmatic KV-cache management for agentic workloads: an orchestrator has trajectory-level context that a single engine cannot infer, while SGLang retains ownership of scheduling, cache allocation, eviction, transfer, and failure handling.

This issue scopes the API boundary needed to carry that intent into SGLang. It does not define a global cache policy or commit SGLang to execute every possible action.

Router-driven KV experiments can use ad-hoc request fields and backend-specific metadata. That is useful scaffolding, but it is not a durable interface for an orchestrator, scheduler, HiCache, or storage backend. We need a typed, versioned envelope that is explicitly request metadata rather than a sampling parameter.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["Trusted router / orchestrator"] --> E["KvHints envelope"]
    E --> I["SGLang request ingress"]
    I --> Q["GenerateReqInput / scheduler Req"]
    Q --> M["KvHintManager"]
    M --> C["Radix cache / HiCache / storage backend"]
    C --> O["Metrics, logs, capability reporting"]
```

## Proposed API

A `kv_hints` value has the following shape:

```json
{
  "protocol_version": "0.1",
  "message_id": "2f82414c-0ab8-4b9e-a806-168d3ad8a1fd",
  "actions": [
    {
      "action_id": "turn-17-demote",
      "action_type": "kv.demote",
      "action_version": "1.0",
      "payload": {
        "session_id": "agent-42",
        "session_generation": 7
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

`kv_hints` is intended to be set by a trusted router after worker selection, not by an untrusted application client.

### Canonical types

The transport types should live in a cache-neutral module, for example `sglang/srt/kv_hints.py`:

```python
class KvHintAction(msgspec.Struct, kw_only=True):
    action_id: str
    action_type: str
    action_version: str
    payload: dict[str, Any]

class KvHints(msgspec.Struct, kw_only=True):
    protocol_version: str
    message_id: str
    actions: list[KvHintAction]
```

- `protocol_version` versions the envelope.
- `message_id` correlates the envelope across router and engine telemetry.
- `action_id` is the idempotency key in the scope defined by its action handler.
- `action_type` is an extensible namespaced name such as `kv.deref`.
- `action_version` versions an individual action independently of the envelope.
- `payload` is interpreted only by the component that implements that action.

The envelope deliberately does not define a closed list of action types. New actions and their payload schemas should land with their implementation and tests.

## Durability guarantees

1. Envelope and action versions evolve independently.
2. Incompatible changes to the envelope or an action payload require a version bump at that layer; optional fields and newly introduced action types do not.
3. Every SGLang request-construction path carries either a canonical `KvHints` value or `None`. `KvHints` is request metadata, never a sampling parameter.
4. Raw ingress rejects an unsupported envelope version or malformed envelope structure.
5. An unsupported action version, disabled capability, or invalid action payload does not prevent independent supported actions in the same envelope from being processed.
6. Action handlers are bounded and fail open: an action may be rejected, clipped, deferred, or ignored, but cannot affect generation correctness or reserve memory indefinitely.

## Propagation

`KvHints` must remain distinct from sampling parameters and flow explicitly through all supported request paths:

```text
HTTP / native gRPC request
  -> GenerateReqInput
  -> tokenization and inter-process request structs
  -> scheduler Req
  -> KvHintManager lifecycle hook
  -> cache- or storage-owned action handler
```

The native protobuf API should carry the same envelope on both text and tokenized generation requests. The Python engine API, HTTP ingress, and gRPC bridge should all construct the same canonical `KvHints` object.

## Initial action implementations

The API is generic, but SGLang already has scaffolding for a small initial set:

| Action | Intended behavior | Required capability |
|---|---|---|
| `kv.deref@1.0` | Release a completed session’s local reusable KV at a request lifecycle boundary. | Session-aware radix cache |
| `kv.demote@1.0` | Publish an eligible session snapshot to configured storage, then make eligible local leaves reclaimable after completion. | Session-aware radix cache + HiCache storage |
| `kv.prefetch@1.0` | Request normal SGLang storage restoration for the current request, including below the usual prefetch threshold. | HiCache storage |

These actions remain advisory. SGLang may reject, clip, defer, or ignore an action because the relevant feature is disabled, the session generation is stale, memory is unavailable, a transfer fails, or the action is unsupported.

An action must never alter correctness: failure falls back to ordinary cache lookup and recomputation.

## Capability discovery and observability

- `/server_info` exposes active capabilities, for example `kv_hint.deref.v1`, `kv_hint.demote.v1`, and `kv_hint.prefetch.v1`.
- Logs, metrics, and traces record accepted, ignored, rejected, duplicate, and completed actions with `message_id` and `action_id`.
- Action count and identifier lengths are bounded.
- Unhinted workloads retain current behavior.

## Implementation plan

1. Land canonical `KvHints` and `KvHintAction` types plus HTTP, engine, scheduler, and gRPC propagation.
2. Add `KvHintManager` as the owner of envelope-version checks, action dispatch, idempotency, capability discovery, and lifecycle hooks.
3. Port the existing typed scaffolding for `kv.deref`, `kv.demote`, and `kv.prefetch`, with focused request-path and cache-state tests.
4. Add end-to-end tests covering HTTP and gRPC equivalence, no-hint compatibility, unsupported versions, unsupported actions, malformed payloads, duplicate actions, disabled capabilities, and storage-failure fallback.
5. Follow with a PR based on [linhu-nv/sglang:linhu/kvcr-hicache-backend](https://github.com/linhu-nv/sglang/tree/linhu/kvcr-hicache-backend), which adds a HiCache/KVCR storage backend for safe cross-instance KV reuse. It is an execution substrate for future remote-fetch/share actions; it should not itself freeze those action semantics.

## Non-goals

- Defining an application-facing replacement for provider-native cache controls.
- Giving a router direct ownership of SGLang scheduler or cache-manager internals.
- Guaranteeing any action executes.
- Defining cross-worker source discovery, storage-key namespace policy, or distributed lifecycle ownership in this transport RFC.
- Adding proactive pre-arrival transfer semantics before their scheduling, admission, and telemetry requirements are specified.

## Related work

- [#27574](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574): programmatic KV-cache policy and taxonomy.
- [#27058](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27058), [#29436](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29436), and [#29173](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29173): merged session identity and session-aware radix-cache substrate.

#### Dynamo – Agentic KV management

- [Dynamo PR #11695](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/11695) established the initial router-to-engine KV-hint prototype. It predates a first-class SGLang `KvHints` transport.
- [Dynamo PR #13134](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13134) defines the typed, versioned router-side KV-hint contract. Once this RFC lands, the Dynamo SGLang adapter should lower that contract directly into SGLang’s `KvHints` envelope at engine ingress rather than using ad-hoc request metadata.

items.title: [RFC] Per-Token-Range KV-Cache Retention Priority
items.body:
## Summary

Today an SGLang request carries a single scalar `priority` applied uniformly to every RadixCache node it touches.  This RFC proposes **per-token-range** retention priority: a request can say "give tokens `[0, 4)` priority 100, leave the rest at default," so KV-cache blocks covering a high-value prefix (e.g. a shared system prompt) are evicted later than lower-priority blocks, independently of the tokens that follow.

This is a **soft ranking, not a hard pin.** Priority orders eviction only among free (unreferenced) blocks: the policy skips any block an active request is using (`lock_ref > 0`) regardless of priority, and among the rest evicts lowest-priority first. A priority-100 block is still evicted if the cache fills and no lower-priority free block remains — think priority queue, not lock.

Note: The design is modeled on TensorRT-LLM's `KvCacheRetentionConfig` / `TokenRangeRetentionConfig`.

## Motivation 

The current eviction policy layers a per-node `priority` on top of an LRU-ish leaf heap (`RadixCache.evict` walks leaves, ranked by `eviction_strategy.get_priority(node)`). Priority is set once per request and `max`-merged along the entire inserted path (`_insert_helper`). Consequences:

- **No intra-request differentiation.** A request cannot mark its system prompt as more valuable than its user turn. The whole sequence shares one priority.
- **Cross-session unfairness.** Nothing stops the engine from evicting Session A's important prefix to make room for Session B's less-important request, even when A matters more — because "importance" is not expressible at sub-request granularity.

TensorRT-LLM solves this with token-range retention: a per-request hint that assigns priorities (and optionally a hold duration) to specific token ranges, consumed per-KV-block by the KV cache manager.

## Goals

- Let a request assign different retention priorities to different token ranges of its prompt.
- Preserve existing behavior when no ranges are supplied.
- Validate malformed input at request entry with a clear error, rather than silently corrupting eviction ordering deep in the cache.

## Non-Goals (this RFC)

- **Priority decay / `duration_ms`.** TRT-LLM (its `durationMs`) lets a priority expire after a duration and fall back to default. Deferred — not because it's unwanted, but because it can't be added cleanly on top of the current tree without its own design pass. Three reasons:
  - **No timer infrastructure.** SGLang's tree has no timer or sweep mechanism today. Decay needs either a lazy check inside `evict()`/`get_priority()` or a background sweep — both new infra, better scoped to their own issue.
  - **It breaks the merge rule.** Each node stores one priority scalar, kept via `max()` across requests. Duration breaks this: if A sets priority 100 for 5s and B sets 50 forever, the node can't track both expiries with one value, and the tree has no memory of who set what. Handling it means redesigning `TreeNode.priority` from a scalar into a list of `(value, expiry)` pairs and rewriting the merge rule — its own design discussion.
  - **It interacts with chunked prefill and node splitting.** Chunked prefill re-enters `_insert_helper` per chunk, and `_split_node` raises a question with no default answer (does a split-created node inherit the parent's remaining duration, or start a fresh clock?). These need a design pass, not inline reuse of the range mechanism.
- **Decode-phase separate priority** (`decodeRetentionPriority`). Deferred.
- **Coverage of every cache backend.** Only the plain `RadixCache` is wired in the prototype (see Backend Coverage).
- **Disk/offload transfer modes** (`transferMode`, `directory`). Out of scope.

## Design

### API shape

A request carries an optional list of token ranges alongside the existing scalar priority. Prototype encoding (a bare tuple):

```python
priority_ranges: Optional[List[Tuple[int, int, int]]]
# each entry: (token_start, token_end_exclusive, priority)
```

Tokens not covered by any range fall back to the scalar `priority`, so existing callers are unaffected. Priority ranges `0-100` (default 35, the TRT-LLM baseline); higher = retained longer. 100 is the ceiling, not a magic value.

The range type uses a named `msgspec.Struct` (per the repo's `no-dataclasses` rule) rather than a positional tuple — named fields are self-documenting, and the struct can absorb future fields ( `duration_ms`) without breaking existing callers. Proposed shape:

```python
class TokenRangeRetention(msgspec.Struct):
    token_start: int
    token_end: Optional[int] = None   # exclusive; None => extend to sequence end
    priority: int = 35                # 0-100, default 35 (TRT-LLM baseline)
```

### Data flow (outside → RadixCache)

The value must survive unchanged from the HTTP/SDK boundary down to the tree:

```
HTTP body / SDK generate(priority_ranges=...)
  -> GenerateReqInput.priority_ranges        (batch: list-of-lists; broadcast: flat)
  -> per-item flatten (__getitem__ / tokenize)
  -> TokenizedGenerateReqInput.priority_ranges   (flat, single request)
  -> IPC
  -> Req.priority_ranges
  -> cache_finished_req / cache_unfinished_req
  -> InsertParams.priority_ranges
  -> RadixCache._insert_helper  (per-segment split)
```

Every layer between the boundary and the tree is currently scalar-shaped, so adding the feature touches all of them; that plumbing is the bulk of the diff.

### Core: boundary-aware insert

Each tree node holds exactly one priority number. A range like "tokens `[0, 4)` get priority 100, the rest stay default" would need two priorities inside one run of tokens — which a single node can't store. The fix is to **cut the tokens into pieces at every point where the priority changes**, and give each piece its own node. Every node still holds one number, so the tree's shape and storage are unchanged; only *where the node boundaries fall* changes.

We introduce two small helpers that decide the cuts:

- `_priority_at(offset, default, ranges)` — answers "what priority applies to the token at this position?" It checks the ranges (first match wins) and falls back to the default when nothing covers it.
- `_range_boundaries_within(node_start, node_len, ranges)` — answers "inside this stretch of tokens, where does the priority flip?" and returns those cut points. Cuts are rounded to a page boundary, because a KV page can't be torn in half.

The two insert paths use these differently:

- **New tokens (fresh suffix).** The suffix is chopped into uniform-priority segments at the cut points, and each segment becomes its own node, chained parent → child. A range with no cuts produces one node — identical to the old single-node insert.
- **Tokens already in the tree (matched prefix).** These nodes aren't re-cut. Each just has its priority bumped to whatever applies at its own start offset, `max`-merged with what's already there — exactly the old behavior, only the merged-in value now varies by position instead of being one flat number.

The matched-prefix path reuses the tree's existing `_split_node` (the same mechanism used when two requests share a partial prefix); the fresh-suffix path builds the segment nodes directly.

### Validation

Malformed ranges are rejected at request entry (`GenerateReqInput.normalize_batch_and_arguments`) with a `ValueError`, before the value threads down to the cache. Strict policy (matches TRT-LLM's constructor-throws behavior):

| Rule | Rejected example |
|------|------------------|
| `start >= 0` | `(-1, 4, 100)` |
| `end > start` (non-empty, non-inverted) | `(5, 5, 100)`, `(8, 3, 100)` |
| priority in `[0, 100]` | `(0, 4, 999)` |
| exactly 3 fields | `(0, 4)` |
| ranges non-overlapping | `[(0, 5, 100), (3, 8, 50)]` |

Gaps are permitted — full coverage is **not** required. Tokens covered by no range use the scalar `priority`; only overlap between ranges is illegal.

Order is **not** part of the contract: overlap is checked on a sorted copy, so an unsorted-but-non-overlapping list is accepted. The caller's list is validated, not mutated — and never reordered downstream either: `_priority_at` scans all ranges and takes the first cover, so it doesn't depend on sort order.

## Backend Coverage

Only the plain `RadixCache` honors `priority_ranges`. The other cache backends (`HiRadixCache`, `SWARadixCache`, `MambaRadixCache`, `UnifiedRadixCache`, `RadixCacheCpp`) each provide their own insert path — overriding `insert()`, `_insert_helper`, or both, and `RadixCacheCpp` inserting through a C++ bridge that takes only `(key, value)` — none of which consumes `priority_ranges`. At most they read the scalar `params.priority` (the cpp bridge doesn't even do that), so they **silently ignore** ranges (graceful degrade, no crash). Extending them is follow-up work and should be scoped per backend.

## Behavioral Notes

- **Mid-page range boundary snaps to the page start, extending the preceding segment's priority forward.** A node can only be split on a page boundary (otherwise KV pages would be torn), so a priority flip that falls mid-page has its split point rounded *down* to the page start (`_range_boundaries_within`: `aligned = (local // page_size) * page_size`). Because each resulting segment takes the priority effective at its own *start* offset (`_priority_at(seg_start)`), snapping the split earlier hands the whole page to the segment that begins at that page start. Worked example (page_size 4, range `[0, 6)` high, default after): the flip at token 6 rounds to a split at token 4, so the segment `[4, 8)` resolves its priority at offset 4 — still inside `[0, 6)` — and the entire page `[4, 8)` becomes high, promoting the out-of-range tokens `[6, 8)`. Net: a mid-page range boundary rounds the higher range's coverage *up* to the page edge.
- **Multi-segment insert emits one KV store event per segment.** A single logical insert that splits into N priority segments fires N `kv_events.record_store` calls instead of one. Each node is genuinely stored, so this is correct, but it is an observable change for KV-event-stream consumers.

## Before Merge

Cleanup this RFC's own prototype needs before it ships — not new features:

1. **`msgspec.Struct` migration** for the range type — replace the positional 3-tuple with the named struct from *Design → API shape* (per the repo's `no-dataclasses` rule).
2. **Tighten `getattr`** — `cache_finished_req` / `cache_unfinished_req` read `getattr(req, "priority_ranges", None)`; the field always exists, so this should be direct attribute access, per the repo's `no-getattr` rule.

## Future Work

Follow-on features, each its own scoped effort. The first three are the deferrals from *Non-Goals*; the entries below say *how* they'd be built.

1. **`duration_ms` / priority decay** — add `priority_expiry_time` to `TreeNode` and factor it into the eviction comparator; fall back to default priority after expiry. (See the *Non-Goals* discussion for why it needs its own design pass first.)
2. **Decode-phase priority** — a separate default for blocks created during generation, letting a request keep its prompt high-priority while decode blocks evict fast.
3. **Backend coverage** — extend `priority_ranges` to HiCache / SWA / Mamba / Unified, scoped per backend (see *Backend Coverage*).
4. **HTTP header surface** — only a scalar `x-override-priority` header exists today; ranges currently must go through the JSON body.

items.title: [RFC] Agent-Aware KV Cache Phase 1 for Agentic Workloads
items.body:
## Summary

This RFC proposes Phase 1 of agent-aware KV cache support in SGLang.

The goal of this phase is to add a minimal, backward-compatible metadata path for agentic workloads so workflow information can flow from the API layer into runtime requests and KV cache nodes, and optionally affect radix cache eviction.

This is intentionally a foundation/prototype phase, not a full workflow-aware cache system.

## Motivation

Current KV cache eviction policies such as LRU, LFU, and SLRU treat requests mostly independently. That works well for standard chat/completion workloads, but it misses reuse opportunities in agentic workflows, where requests often share:

- repeated prompt prefixes across planner/tool/worker steps
- parent/child step relationships
- short-term reuse after tool calls
- workflow-level TTL or reuse intent

Without workflow-aware signals, cache entries that are likely to be reused by upcoming steps may be evicted too early.

## Proposal

Phase 1 introduces:

- an optional `agent_hints` field in OpenAI-compatible requests
- propagation of `agent_hints` through the internal request pipeline
- lightweight workflow DAG tracking in the scheduler
- radix cache node annotation with workflow metadata
- a new optional radix eviction policy: `agent_aware`

Initial `agent_hints` fields include:

- `workflow_id`
- `agent_id`
- `step_id`
- `step_index`
- `total_steps`
- `parent_step_id`
- `children_step_ids`
- `tool_name`
- `expected_tool_duration_ms`
- `cache_ttl_ms`
- `shared_prefix_hash`
- `reuse_hint`

## Scope

Phase 1 is intended to cover:

- request schema support
- metadata plumbing
- scheduler-side workflow tracking
- cache node metadata annotation
- a prototype workflow-aware eviction strategy

Phase 1 does **not** attempt to fully solve:

- `shared_prefix_hash`-driven reuse
- HiCache / storage-layer metadata inheritance
- cross-process workflow coordination
- production-tuned scoring for all agent topologies

## Backward Compatibility

- `agent_hints` is optional
- existing clients do not need to change
- existing eviction policies continue to work unchanged
- the new behavior is opt-in

## Testing

Expected validation for Phase 1:

- schema tests for `agent_hints`
- propagation tests from API request to internal request objects
- workflow DAG tests for step registration and distance computation
- radix cache node annotation tests
- eviction ordering tests for `agent_aware`
- backward-compat tests when `agent_hints` is omitted

How to Run
Start SGLang with the new eviction policy:
```
curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "default",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
    "agent_hints": {
      "workflow_id": "wf-1",
      "agent_id": "planner",
      "step_id": "step-1",
      "children_step_ids": ["step-2"],
      "cache_ttl_ms": 60000,
      "reuse_hint": "keep"
    }
  }'
```

Prototype validation already exists with dedicated unit tests for the metadata path.

## Open Questions

- Should `shared_prefix_hash` remain a hint, or become a stronger reuse primitive in a later phase?
- Should TTL be a hard protection or only a ranking signal?
- How should workflow-aware metadata eventually interact with HiCache and storage backends?
- What observability should be added next: workflow hit rate, protected eviction count, step-distance metrics?

## Requested Feedback

Feedback is especially useful on:

- the proposed `agent_hints` schema
- whether scheduler-local DAG tracking is the right Phase 1 boundary
- whether `agent_aware` should land as an experimental eviction policy first
- what should be included in Phase 2
