items.title: [RFC] linker: Prefetch SSD-resident KV while the request is queued
items.body:
## TL;DR

When a request hits KV that sits on SSD, the direct linker reads it **inside the batch forward**, so the whole batch waits for the SSD. This RFC moves that SSD read to **while the request is still queued**: the storage backend copies the KV from SSD to its DRAM, and the request is admitted once the copy is done.

## Flow

Red blocks are new; everything else exists today.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant C as Client / router
    participant S as Scheduler
    participant L as Linker
    participant St as Mooncake / UMBP
    participant F as GPU forward

    rect rgb(255, 224, 224)
        Note over C,S: NEW (later phase): hint before the request arrives
        C->>S: prefetch hint (agent session resuming, e.g. tool call returned)
    end

    C->>S: request

    rect rgb(255, 224, 224)
        Note over S,St: NEW: look up and start prefetch at enqueue
        S->>L: lookup(rid, prefetch=True)
        L->>St: batch exist, prefetch_to_memory
        St-->>L: hit pages (some only on SSD)
        St->>St: copy SSD-only pages to DRAM (async, read lease)
    end

    rect rgb(255, 224, 224)
        Note over S,St: NEW: request waits in queue until its KV is in DRAM
        loop every scheduling round
            S->>L: prefetch_status(rid)
            L->>St: pages in DRAM?
            St-->>L: not yet / yes
            L-->>S: PENDING / READY
        end
        Note over S: skip PENDING requests (prefetch policy and timeout)
    end

    S->>L: load_back at admission
    S->>F: run batch
    F->>L: start layer-wise loading
    L->>St: ranged gets
    St-->>F: KV from DRAM into the device pool (RDMA)
```

Steps 1 and 3-10 are new. Today the lookup happens only at admission, and if the hit is on SSD, step 15 reads it from SSD inside the forward while the whole batch waits.

For scale, GLM-5.2-FP8 on 8xH200 with a 64K cached prefix: a hit served from Mooncake DRAM costs 263-384 ms of TTFT, a cold prefill 5.6 s. The same prefix is about 6.6 GB per rank, so serving it from a single NVMe drive inside the forward would stall the batch for seconds.

## Why not HiCache

HiCache already prefetches into a host pool managed by the radix tree. The deployments here cannot afford that host pool on the inference node, which is why they use the linker. This RFC keeps the data in the **storage backend's** DRAM instead of adding an engine-side cache.

## Who does what

| | Today | New |
|---|---|---|
| **Client / router** | sends the request | (later) sends a prefetch hint as soon as it knows an agent session will resume |
| **Scheduler** | looks up the external cache at admission | looks up at enqueue with `prefetch=True`; skips requests whose prefetch is `PENDING`, reusing `--hicache-storage-prefetch-policy` (`best_effort` / `wait_complete` / `timeout`) |
| **Linker** | `lookup`, `load`, layer-wise loading | `lookup(..., prefetch=True)` and `prefetch_status(rid)`; both are no-ops by default, so backends without prefetch behave as today |
| **Mooncake** | serves reads from DRAM or SSD | copies SSD-only hits to DRAM on `exist` (`ExistOptions(prefetch_to_memory=True)`, kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4272, open) and reports whether keys have a DRAM replica |
| **UMBP** | direct linker requires `ssd_enabled=false` | needs SSD support on the direct path plus an equivalent SSD-to-DRAM promotion |

No change to the radix tree or to the device-side load path.

## Later

- The client / router prefetch hint (step 1), aligned with the orchestrator `PREFETCH` hint in #43098.
- If a backend has no DRAM tier, optionally put a small local DRAM buffer in front of it (#44916).

## Open questions

1. Is the store's DRAM on the inference node or on separate memory nodes?
2. How cheap is checking readiness every scheduling round?
3. What should happen when the store's DRAM is full and promotion fails?

Related: #43098, #45106, #44916, kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4272.

items.title: [RFC] scheduler: Overlap prefill scheduling and KV loading with model execution
items.body:
**Implementation status:** local runtime integration, CPU regressions and initial PD experiments have been performed against main base 92580581da. The implementation is not pushed; the Draft PR still has an intentionally empty diff. Supporting authoring files remain local. Further investigation and validation are continuing. **Implementation tracker:** https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44723 (Draft; local integration under validation). ## Motivation Native overlap already overlaps some CPU work with GPU execution, but the scheduler regains control only after its synchronous CPU model call returns. Preparing the next batch and submitting cached-KV loads can therefore happen late. Agent requests arriving during that call create additional useful work to advance. We propose one persistent forward thread while the scheduler remains the only owner of requests, radix state, allocation, admission, and retirement. A = current batch, B = next batch, C = an earlier batch. ```mermaid %%{init: {"theme": "base", "gantt": {"displayMode": "compact", "barHeight": 30, "barGap": 8, "fontSize": 13, "sectionFontSize": 14, "leftPadding": 190, "rightPadding": 45}, "themeVariables": {"taskBkgColor": "#dff2e8", "taskBorderColor": "#318463", "taskTextColor": "#172b4d", "activeTaskBkgColor": "#fff0bb", "activeTaskBorderColor": "#ba8a20", "critBkgColor": "#ffe5e5", "critBorderColor": "#bd5656", "doneTaskBkgColor": "#e4edff", "doneTaskBorderColor": "#3b6bb5", "sectionBkgColor": "#f7f9fc", "sectionBkgColor2": "#eff7f2", "sectionBkgColor3": "#f7f9fc", "taskTextDarkColor": "#172b4d", "taskTextOutsideColor": "#172b4d", "gridColor": "#d8e0e9"}}}%% gantt title Move preparation and KV loading into A's model-call window dateFormat YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss axisFormat %S tickInterval 10second todayMarker off section Native / Scheduler Prep A : a0, 2026-01-01T00:00:00, 5s CPU model call A : done, a1, 2026-01-01T00:00:05, 20s Retire C / prepare B : a2, 2026-01-01T00:00:25, 12s CPU call B : done, a3, 2026-01-01T00:00:40, 10s section Native / GPU A forward window : active, a4, 2026-01-01T00:00:07, 21s Exposed boundary : crit, a5, 2026-01-01T00:00:28, 14s B forward : active, a6, 2026-01-01T00:00:42, 8s section Native / B KV Load B : a7, 2026-01-01T00:00:32, 12s section V2 / Scheduler Prep A : b0, 2026-01-01T00:00:00, 5s Retire C : b1, 2026-01-01T00:00:06, 6s Receive : b2, 2026-01-01T00:00:12, 7s Prepare B : b3, 2026-01-01T00:00:19, 6s Handoff : b4, 2026-01-01T00:00:25, 5s section V2 / Forward worker CPU model call A : done, b5, 2026-01-01T00:00:05, 20s CPU call B : done, b6, 2026-01-01T00:00:30, 10s section V2 / GPU A forward window : active, b7, 2026-01-01T00:00:07, 21s Gap : crit, b8, 2026-01-01T00:00:28, 4s B forward : active, b9, 2026-01-01T00:00:32, 8s section V2 / B KV Early load B : b10, 2026-01-01T00:00:21, 12s ``` *Horizontal positions are schematic, in arbitrary units. Widths are not measured durations or continuous GPU activity. B consumes KV as the required layers become ready.* **One state owner, separate execution and loading paths** ```mermaid %%{init: {"theme": "base", "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": true, "curve": "linear", "nodeSpacing": 35, "rankSpacing": 55}, "themeVariables": {"fontFamily": "Arial, sans-serif", "fontSize": "15px", "lineColor": "#7a8699", "edgeLabelBackground": "#ffffff", "clusterBkg": "#f7f9fc", "clusterBorder": "#d8e0e9"}, "fontFamily": "Arial, sans-serif"}}%% flowchart LR accTitle: One scheduler owner, separate forward and KV loading paths S["Scheduler owner
Retire C and prepare B
Only writer of shared state"] F["Forward worker
A model call
Kernel submission"] L["KV backend
HiCache / Mooncake
Load B's cached KV"] subgraph GPU["GPU"] A["A forward
Compute + communication"] B["B cached KV
Per-layer readiness"] end S -->|Run A| F S -->|Load B| L F -->|Kernels| A L -->|Transfer| B classDef owner fill:#dff2e8,stroke:#318463,stroke-width:2px,color:#172b4d classDef worker fill:#e4edff,stroke:#3b6bb5,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d classDef load fill:#eee5ff,stroke:#8159ba,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d classDef compute fill:#fff0bb,stroke:#ba8a20,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d class S owner class F worker class L,B load class A compute style GPU fill:#f7f9fc,stroke:#d8e0e9,stroke-width:1px,color:#596579 ``` ## Proposed changes - Overlap current-batch **A** execution with independent previous-batch **C** retirement/PD completion and next-batch **B** intake, bootstrap, preparation, and cached-KV loading. - Keep frozen per-batch loading dependencies and rank-consistent owner progress; complete owner preparation before EAGLE Draft uses shared TP/MoE state. - Fully prepare independent B batches. HiCache also supports bounded KV-only warming during an active chunk; Mooncake chunk-follower warming remains disabled. - Reuse HiCache transfer protections and preserve request-private loading, cancellation, and failure semantics for Mooncake direct linker. - Use the proposed default-off switch, `--enable-overlap-schedule-v2`, with existing backend selection. The switch is not available in upstream main yet. The current implementation advances eligible work during A's CPU model call; it does **not** limit work to explicit GPU-feedback waits. Ownership, pins and fences protect correctness; they do not make Python steps preemptible or eliminate GIL, driver and bandwidth interference. Measurements must include any increase in A's submission time. ## Initial main-port results At concurrency 20, two runs per flag show **5.04% higher input throughput with HiCache** and **6.28% with Mooncake**, with mean run-level median TTFT reduced by **11.04%** and **10.67%**, respectively. **P99 is not consistently improved.** These are initial local results; paired measurements are in [Feat Draft PR #44723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44723). ### Test configuration GLM-5.3 FP8; separate **8×H200 Prefill** and **8×H200 Decode** nodes. Selected flags from our test setup are shown below; these are configuration excerpts, not full reproduction commands. **Prefill — common to both cache backends** ```bash --disaggregation-mode prefill --tp-size 8 --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --enable-dsa-cache-layer-split --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --prefill-max-requests 8 --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 524288 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled ``` **Cache backend — choose one** ```bash # HiCache host L2: about 256 GiB of host-cache payload --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-host-memory-mode cache --hicache-ratio 3.5465017306928446 --hicache-mem-layout layer_first --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-write-policy write_through # Or Mooncake direct linker: 32 GiB per P rank, about 256 GiB total --enable-unified-cache-external-linker --unified-cache-external-linker-backend mooncake # Storage config: protocol=rdma, global_segment_size=32gb per rank; # master address and device names are deployment-specific. ``` **Decode — unchanged between OFF and ON** ```bash --disaggregation-mode decode --tp-size 8 --attn-dp-size 8 --enable-dp-lm-head --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --enable-hisparse --hisparse-config '{"top_k":2048,"device_buffer_size":12288,"host_to_device_ratio":8}' ``` **OFF / ON:** native Prefill overlap remains enabled in both. ON adds `--enable-overlap-schedule-v2` to P; OFF omits it. HiCache ON also uses the bounded demand-transfer policy, so its result measures the combined feature. **Workload:** - Public Weka 256K traces: **80 root sessions**, seed `20261016`; **21 historical warmup requests**, then **903 formal requests**, all completed without errors. - Same formal payloads: **52,867,171 input tokens** and **16 output tokens/request**. Closed-loop HTTP concurrency **20 or 10**; session/subagent dependencies are preserved and slots release after the full response. - Same configured L1 and backing-cache capacities; total token cache hit is about **88.83%**. Formal prompts are not replayed for warmup; actual grouping and small cache-replacement differences can vary. **Draft status:** the results support the proposed overlap direction. Detailed trace analysis, final reproduction commands, and broader validation will be added once the implementation is finalized. Mooncake here uses P-host cache segments; cross-host cache scaling and HiCache L2 + Mooncake L3 are outside this measurement. ## Implementation plan 1. Finalize and review the local owner/worker and backend implementation while retaining main's lifecycle protections. 2. Complete model/numerical and failure/cancellation coverage, and investigate tail-latency regressions. 3. Publish the verified runtime patch and reproduction commands; extend testing to other supported deployments. Initial targets are text-only CUDA PD prefill, PP1/DCP1, disabled CUDA graphs and the CP8 DSA layer-split/EAGLE reference configuration. Independent DP replicas and other feature combinations require further validation. ## Related resources - [Feat Draft PR #44723](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44723). - Reviewed main base: [92580581da](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/92580581da6fc8542a997a00c1a8b71b03497680).

items.title: [RFC] KVCR as a HiCacheStorage backend for peer-to-peer KV reuse
items.body:
## Summary SGLang's HiCache already supports pluggable L3 storage backends (mooncake, hf3fs, eic, …) behind a stable `HiCacheStorage` interface. This RFC adds KVCR as one more such backend. KVCR is a multi-tier KV cache management solution from NVIDIA. The integration totally follows the integration and design of hicache storage — we register a `"kvcr"` backend and implement the same `batch_set_v2 / batch_get_v2 / batch_exists_v2` contract the other backends already implement. This backend also aligns with the router-initiated hint model in **[#27574 — Programmatic KV Cache for Agentic Workloads](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574)**, which defines a provider-neutral hint taxonomy (Share / Prefetch / Demote / Pin / Retain). KVCR fits the **`Share`** intent — *"reuse a prefix that already lives on another worker... pull the prefix from the old one"* — but does not depend on that RFC: it is a self-contained mechanism any router emitting such a hint can drive. Following the Dynamo DEP (ai-dynamo/dynamo#11673), the near term goal is **direct worker-to-worker (host memory) KV reuse**: a prefix computed on one worker is served to another without recomputation or a round-trip through a global pool. When a request lands on a worker lacking a prefix another worker holds, KVCR fetches it **peer-to-peer** — an asymmetric, directed transfer, not a symmetric external store. Selecting *which* peer holds the prefix is a decision only a router can make well. So the router hands the target worker a small piece of per-request metadata — a **hint** — naming the peer. "Router" here means any orchestrator above the engine: the router (flash indexer) is the first target, SGLang's own router a later one, and the same carrier serves both. The rest of this RFC covers (1) that hint and (2) how KVCR plugs into HiCache to act on it. ## Part 1 — Router Hint ### Why a hint is needed HiCache storage is content-addressed: the controller asks `get(block_hash)` and the backend is expected to know where the bytes live. That works for a global pool. It does **not** work for P2P reuse, where the same prefix may sit on any one of N peer workers. The only component that knows which one is the **router** — it made the routing decision that sent this request here in the first place. The hint will directly tell the node where target kvcache sits. ### Why decide this at the router Putting the source-selection decision at the routing stage — rather than probing peers after a request lands — is what makes the hint valuable beyond avoiding a broadcast: - **It enables a routing cost function that can grow over time.** The hint is the input to a decision the router makes; that decision can start *simple* (route on load only, ignoring cache residency) and evolve to *rich* (weigh prefix cache residency, estimated transfer time, distance/topology, and thresholds that decide when a P2P fetch is even worth it versus recomputation). - **It lets us prefetch and shape system behavior.** Because the router decides before the request is admitted, the target can begin fetching the prefix ahead of time, and the router — with its global view — can steer placement to balance load and reuse across the fleet, rather than reacting locally after the fact. ### Carrier We do **not** widen the `HiCacheStorage` signature. Every v2 call already threads a free-form `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info` dict from the controller into the backend. The hint is the `Share` case of #27574's provider-neutral hint envelope and rides in that dict; the key name below is a placeholder pending #27574's envelope: ``` # placeholder key — to be aligned with #27574's KvHintEnvelope extra_info.extra_info["kvcr_router_hint"] = { "source_control_endpoint": "host:port", # ZMQ control endpoint of the peer holding the prefix "block_hashes": [...], # root-aligned block hashes for the shared prefix } ``` ### Propagation path The hint travels from the router down to the backend without widening any interface — it rides the `extra_info` dict every layer already passes through: 1. **router → scheduler.** The router attaches the hint to the request's `extra_info`; the scheduler stashes it into the prefetch request. 2. **scheduler → controller.** `HiCacheController.prefetch(...)` carries it into the daemon `prefetch_io_aux_func` thread (`managers/cache_controller.py`). 3. **controller → backend.** `_page_transfer → page_get_func(op, hashes, host_idx, extra_info)` hands it to `KVCR.batch_get_v2(...)` (`storage/kvcr/kvcr_store.py`). 4. **backend → decision.** `RouterHint.maybe_from_extra_info(extra_info)` (`storage/kvcr/router_hint.py`) parses it: - hint **absent/malformed** → fall back to local-only (deposit/local-get), never raises; - hint **present** → drive a directed P2P fetch from `source_control_endpoint`. The parser is **fail-closed**: a missing or malformed hint degrades to local-only behavior, it never crashes a prefetch, and the backend is safe to ship before the any router side lands (dynamo pr here https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/11695). ## Part 2 — KVCR Integration Architecture ### Where it sits ```mermaid flowchart LR SCH[Scheduler] --- HRC[HiRadixCache] --- HCC[HiCacheController] HCC -->|HiCacheStorage iface| KS[KVCR
thin adapter] subgraph core[KVCR core · vendored] LD[local DRAM tier
deposit / get] CC[control channel
ZMQ peer] PT[progress thread
owns NIXL agent] end KS --> core ``` `KVCR` is a thin adapter. It owns no transfer threads of its own — kvcr's core runs **one** daemon "kvcr-progress" thread that exclusively holds the NIXL agent and control socket. The store advances state only by calling `poll_completed()` from the HiCache controller's existing prefetch thread. No new threading model is introduced into SGLang. ### Get path (with router hint) — sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant AUX as prefetch aux thread participant KS as KVCR participant PT as KVCR progress thread participant SRC as source worker participant SCH as scheduler AUX->>KS: batch_get_v2(hashes, host_idx, extra_info) Note over KS: hint = maybe_from_extra_info(...) KS->>PT: submit_hint(source_endpoint, keys) Note over PT: register source peer KS->>PT: h = deliver(blocks) PT->>SRC: START_WRITE (ctrl) Note over SRC: search_and_pin SRC-->>PT: NIXL WRITE (UCX) → host pages (direct DMA) SRC-->>PT: send_notif("write_done") Note over PT: _poll_notifications
_TargetDeliverOp: WAITING→FINISHED PT-->>KS: _completion_queue.append(OpResult) Note over KS: poll_completed(): match r.op_handle == h KS-->>AUX: [per-page success bools] Note over AUX: operation.increment(page_size × hits) SCH->>SCH: check_prefetch_progress(req_id)
polls completed_tokens (hiradix_cache.py) Note over SCH: True → req admitted into batch ``` - **A single KVCR daemon thread owns the whole P2P mechanism.** It handles all KVCR↔KVCR message send/recv, maintains the internal op state machine, and drives the interaction with NIXL transfers. When a transfer finishes it does not push anything — it just appends the result to a completion queue; the store itself spawns no extra thread. - **The KVCR thread never touches the scheduler main thread or the prefetch thread.** It runs entirely on its own, so neither of SGLang's threads is blocked or slowed by how KVCR does its work. - **The existing completion-notification model is unchanged.** A finished transfer sits on that queue until the prefetch daemon thread actively drains it via `poll_completed()` and turns it into `completed_tokens`; the scheduler main thread, one level up, only reads the resulting boolean tick (`check_prefetch_progress`) — the same KVPoll-style poll as today. ### Non-goals - No changes to HiRadixCache or the scheduler cache path. - No new SGLang-side transfer threads. - Shared-HiCache serving (source pins from HiRadixCache via `TreeNode.protect_host`) is a future swap of the pin adapter only — out of scope here.

items.title: [RFC] Align KV cache events with vLLM's schema so shared consumers have a standard format
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

# Motivation

## Summary

#37482 switched KV cache events to tagged msgpack maps, the same encoding vLLM moved to in vllm-project/vllm#42892. The fields both engines have use the same names. A consumer however can't treat events from both engines in a standard fashion because of the following:

1. Replay responses are missing the topic frame vLLM added in vllm-project/vllm#45177.
2. There's no `lora_name` in SGLang events. vLLM always sends it and its msgspec types reject events without it.
3. The salt is in a `cache_salt` field in SGLang. vLLM puts it in `extra_keys` on block 0 which is where a consumer like llm-d looks for it.
4. Event hashes leave out `extra_key` in SGLang, so LoRA and base model blocks with the same tokens share a hash.

This RFC proposes fixing those four in SGLang's native format in three phases to align with vLLM for standardization. It doesn't propose a vLLM hash mode or a format flag. Consumers like llm-d don't need vLLM's hash recipe and the in-repo router depends on SGLang's.

## Background

### What already matches

| Area | SGLang and vLLM |
|---|---|
| Event encoding | Tagged maps, class name under `type`, `None` optionals omitted |
| Batch | Positional `[ts, events, dp_rank]` |
| Live frames | `(topic, seq, payload)` |
| `BlockStored` fields | `block_hashes`, `parent_block_hash`, `token_ids`, `block_size`, `lora_id`, `medium`, `session_id` |
| `BlockRemoved`, `AllBlocksCleared` | Same, apart from vLLM's optional `group_idx` |

### Consumers checked

| Consumer | How it reads SGLang events |
|---|---|
| llm-d `engineType: sglang` | Positional arrays only. It can't read anything since #37482. That's llm-d's to fix |
| llm-d `engineType: vllm` | Reads SGLang's maps today. Derives its own block keys from `token_ids`, `lora_name` and `extra_keys` and uses engine hashes only as opaque keys |
| `experimental/sgl-router` | Decodes SGLang maps and ignores unknown keys. Recomputes SGLang's hash recipe on the request side (`kv_events/hash.rs`). Decodes hashes as `i64`. Maps `medium` strings to tiers |
| sgl-router replay client (#32729, open) | Parses today's two frame replay reply |
| vLLM's msgspec types | Fail on SGLang events (see below) |

Dynamo wasn't checked.

## Gaps

### 1. Replay replies have no topic frame

| | Replayed batch | End marker |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM | `(client_id, b"", topic, seq, payload)` | `(client_id, b"", b"", END_SEQ, b"")` |
| SGLang (`kv_events.py:541,546`) | `(client_id, b"", seq, payload)` | `(client_id, b"", END_SEQ, b"")` |

llm-d's replay client requires three frames after the delimiter (`parseEventFrame` in `pkg/kvevents/zmq_subscriber.go`). From reading that code: with `replaySocketPort` set for an SGLang pool, every replay
is rejected as malformed and the pod's index entries are cleared. Live batches that arrive before a successful replay are dropped and the retry 30 seconds later fails the same way, so the pod never gets indexed.

### 2. No `lora_name`

vLLM declares `lora_id`, `medium` and `lora_name` without defaults, so all three are always on the wire. Decoding a SGLang batch with vLLM's struct definitions (copied from `vllm/distributed/kv_events.py` at `de24e51908`) fails:

```
msgspec.ValidationError: Object missing required field `lora_name` - at `$[1][0]`
```

The reverse direction works. llm-d also uses `lora_name` as the model name when it derives keys, so SGLang LoRA blocks are indexed as base model blocks.

### 3. The salt isn't in `extra_keys`

vLLM sends one `extra_keys` entry per block: LoRA name, multimodal identifiers, then `cache_salt` only on the block starting at token 0. llm-d reads the salt only from there. Its precise prefix cache README says salted SGLang requests "are precise-cache misses until SGLang emits `extra_keys`". Unsalted requests can also score hits against salted only copies. SGLang still isolates the cache, so this costs routing quality, not safety.

A side note that corrects the earlier #27682 discussion: vLLM's hashes are salt namespaced too because the salt in block 0's extra keys is part of the hash. Neither engine has `BlockRemoved` ambiguity across salts.

### 4. Event hashes leave out `extra_key`

`compute_node_event_hash_values` (`mem_cache/utils.py:178`) seeds the chain with the salt only. `Req` folds the LoRA uuid into `extra_key` (`schedule_batch.py:1096-1099`). So from reading the code, a LoRA block and a base model block with the same tokens emit the same hash and a `BlockRemoved` for one looks like a removal of both. Storage hashes already include the namespace (`storage_namespace_seed`, `utils.py:125`). vLLM includes the LoRA name in its block hash.

## Proposal

### Phase 1: additive fields, no consumer breaks

**1a. `lora_name`, with `medium` required.** Use vLLM's field order:

```python
class BlockStored(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    parent_block_hash: Optional[int]
    token_ids: list[int]
    block_size: int
    lora_id: Optional[int]
    medium: Optional[str]
    lora_name: Optional[str]
    extra_keys: Optional[list[Optional[tuple]]] = None
    cache_salt: Optional[str] = None
    session_id: Optional[str] = None


class BlockRemoved(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    medium: Optional[str]
```

msgspec needs `medium` to lose its default so that `lora_name` is always sent. Every constructor already passes `medium`. `lora_name` stays `null` until phase 3. `lora_id` stays `null` because vLLM's is a deprecated int and SGLang's is a uuid string.

**1b. `extra_keys` with the salt.** When a node's parent is the root (its first page starts at token 0) and `cache_salt` is set, send `extra_keys=[(salt,), None, ...]` lined up with `block_hashes`. `KVCacheEventRecorder.enqueue` merges parent linked stores and would extend `extra_keys` the same way. The Rust tree core's tagged tuple (`rust_tree_core/adapter.py:85`) needs the field too. Keep `cache_salt`. It's documented and vLLM decoders ignore it.

Effect: vLLM typed decoders read SGLang and llm-d routes salted SGLang traffic correctly. sgl-router ignores both keys.

### Phase 2: replay topic frame

Send `self._topic_bytes` before the sequence number in replay replies and `b""` before `END_SEQ`. That's the vLLM layout.

Replay clients should accept both layouts: two frames after the delimiter is `[seq, payload]`, three is
`[topic, seq, payload]`. Then a new router works with old and new workers. Neither in-repo client has shipped: #32729 is open and #39610's example is open. So they can take the dual parse before this lands and only external clients written against the two frame layout would break.

### Phase 3: LoRA name and namespaced event hashes

These two go together. Adding `lora_name` without the hash change would give llm-d two keys for one engine hash.

**3a.** Carry the adapter name to the tree node, either as a `RadixKey` field or through a lookup in the scheduler's LoRA manager. Fill `lora_name`. With LoRA, put the name first in each `extra_keys` entry, as vLLM does.

**3b.** When `extra_key` is set, seed event hashes with the full namespace, the same way storage hashes do. Keep the current `sglang-cache-salt-v1` seed when only a salt is set, so salted hashes don't change. Mirror it in the Rust tree core.

**sgl-router cost:** its request side hash has no namespace. Today LoRA requests match base model blocks which can't be reused anyway. After 3b they match nothing until the router hashes with the namespace. That's a follow-up in `kv_events/hash.rs`.

### Not proposed

- **Renaming `CPU_PINNED` to `CPU`.** llm-d weights unknown tier names like GPU, so `cpu_pinned` scores 1.0 instead of 0.8. But sgl-router drops stores whose `medium` it doesn't know (`Tiers::for_store`, `kv_events/tree.rs`), so a  rename would turn off host-tier routing on older routers. llm-d users can set `kvCacheBackendConfigs: [{name: cpu_pinned, weight: 0.8}]` instead. See open question 1.
- **Unsigned hashes.** vLLM sends unsigned 64-bit and SGLang sends signed. llm-d accepts both (llm-d-router#2601 widens that). sgl-router decodes `i64`, so flipping would break it.
- **A vLLM hash recipe or `--kv-events-format vllm`.** llm-d doesn't recompute engine hashes and sgl-router depends on SGLang's recipe. Two formats would be a second thing to test with no consumer asking for it.
- **`group_idx` / `kv_cache_spec_kind`.** llm-d indexes events without `group_idx` as-is. Sending `group_idx` without a kind would make llm-d skip every store.

## Compatibility

| Change | vLLM-typed decoders | llm-d `vllm` adapter | sgl-router (main) | sgl-router replay (#32729) | #39610 docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1a `lora_name`, required `medium` | Fixed | No change until phase 3 | Ignored | n/a | Add field |
| 1b `extra_keys` salt | Reads it | Salted routing fixed | Ignored | n/a | Add field |
| 2 Replay topic frame | n/a | Replay works | n/a | Needs dual parse | Update example |
| 3a `lora_name` filled | Reads it | LoRA indexed under adapter name | Ignored | n/a | Update |
| 3b Namespaced hashes | n/a | `BlockRemoved` unambiguous | LoRA misses until router follow-up | n/a | Note |

## Out of scope

- **Multimodal.** SGLang replaces image tokens with hash derived pad values, so `token_ids` differ from vLLM's placeholders. `extra_keys` can't fix that.
- **EAGLE bigram `token_ids`.** Tracked separately.
- **Pages smaller than llm-d's block size** (llm-d-router#2235).
- **A removal reason on `BlockRemoved`** (#39604). It's additive but it would be worth proposing to vLLM too so the schemas don't drift again.

## Open questions

1. **Tier names.** Keep `CPU_PINNED` and document the llm-d weight? Or have sgl-router accept `CPU` first and switch the engine a release later?
2. **LoRA name source.** A `RadixKey` field which also needs the Rust core or a scheduler side lookup?
3. **LoRA in `extra_keys`.** llm-d's `ParseRawExtraKeys` reads bare strings as multimodal hashes which looks like it would fold a vLLM `lora_name` into keys the request side never adds. That isn't verified. Should SGLang match vLLM anyway or wait until llm-d settles it?
4. **Snapshots.** Should snapshot payloads from #33394 / #34407 use the same event schema?


# Related resources

- #27682: original request for `cache_salt` in `extra_keys`
- #37482: tagged-map events, `cache_salt` and `session_id` fields
- #39610: KV events docs page (open)
- #32729: sgl-router KV event gap replay (open)
- #33394, #34407: recoverable KV placement state with snapshots
- #39604: removal reason on `BlockRemoved`
- vllm-project/vllm#42892: vLLM events switched to maps
- vllm-project/vllm#45177: topic frame in vLLM replay replies
- vllm-project/vllm#51381: `session_id` on vLLM `BlockStored`
- llm-d/llm-d-router `pkg/kvevents/engineadapter/vllm_adapter.go`: map aware decoder SGLang events already pass through
- llm-d/llm-d-router#2235: pages smaller than the llm-d block size
- llm-d/llm-d-router#2601: hash integer conversion

items.title: [RFC][sgl-router] Recoverable KV Placement State with Snapshots and Event Replay
items.body: ## Background KV-aware routing relies on an accurate view of which KV blocks are available on each KV cache replica. Today, the Router builds this view incrementally from live `BlockStored` and `BlockRemoved` events. This works when the Router starts before the Workers and receives every event, but it cannot reliably recover when: - the Router or KV Indexer starts after caches have already been populated; - the placement-state consumer—either the Router’s embedded index or an external KV Indexer—restarts, loses its in-memory placement view, and must reconstruct it from replica snapshots before safely serving cache-aware routing decisions; - events are lost because of backpressure, network interruption, or subscriber restart; - a KV cache replica restarts and its previous placement state becomes invalid; - an event gap is older than the replay buffer. These cases do not affect inference correctness, but they may leave the placement view incomplete or stale, resulting in suboptimal routing and lower KV cache hit rates. ## Proposal Each independently routable KV cache replica should provide: - a **live event stream** for steady-state updates; - a **replay journal** for repairing short event gaps; - a **snapshot endpoint** for initialization and full recovery. The replica is identified by the same Worker endpoint and DP or attention-DP rank used by the existing KV-event subscription. No additional cache-group abstraction is introduced. ## Tensor Parallelism A KV cache replica may contain multiple TP ranks. KV tensors are physically sharded across those ranks, while their logical block hashes and block lifecycle are expected to remain synchronized. For example: ```text TP=4, DP=1 → 1 KV cache replica → 1 snapshot TP=4, DP=2 → 2 KV cache replicas → 2 snapshots ``` The Router selects a replica, not an individual TP rank. Therefore, one logical snapshot is exposed per replica rather than one snapshot per TP rank. A designated metadata leader, currently equivalent to: ```text pp_rank == 0 attn_tp_rank == 0 attn_cp_rank == 0 ``` represents the replica and owns: - snapshot generation; - event sequencing; - replay retention; - live event publication. This follows the ownership model already used by the current KV event publisher and avoids duplicate snapshots from TP ranks. ## Snapshot Semantics Each replica maintains: - `epoch`: changes whenever the replica is restarted or rebuilt; - `seq`: monotonically increases within one epoch. The epoch should be assigned by the replica lifecycle owner and propagated to the metadata publisher, rather than being generated only by the metadata leader. If any required TP rank is restarted or replaced, the replica must use a new epoch, even if the metadata leader itself did not restart. A snapshot contains: ```text worker endpoint dp_rank or attn_dp_rank epoch resume_seq active block records ``` Each active block record must include the parent relationship required to rebuild the placement index. The format may reuse `BlockStored`-compatible records: ```text parent_block_hash block_hashes ``` An equivalent chain representation is also acceptable as long as the consumer can reconstruct the same logical prefix tree. The consistency requirement is: > A snapshot with `resume_seq = N` reflects the effects of all placement events with sequence numbers smaller than `N`. Events starting from `N` can be recovered from the replay journal or live event stream. The snapshot contains placement metadata only. It does not transfer KV tensors. ## Architecture The placement-state consumer may be the Router’s embedded HashTree or an external KV Indexer. ## Main Flow During initialization or full recovery, the consumer: 1. Subscribes to the live event stream and buffers incoming events. 2. Fetches the replica snapshot. 3. Builds a staging placement view from the snapshot block records. 4. Replays events starting from `resume_seq`. 5. Applies buffered live events in sequence order and verifies that no sequence gap remains. 6. Atomically publishes the recovered view and marks the replica as `READY`. Snapshot, replay, and live events are independent inputs to the synchronization controller. They are not processed as a serial pipeline. Only `READY` replica views are used for cache-aware routing. During steady-state operation, live events are applied incrementally using `(epoch, seq)` for ordering and deduplication. ## Recovery Behavior - **Sequence gap:** stop using the affected replica for cache-aware routing and request replay from the missing sequence. - **Replay unavailable:** discard the affected view and fetch a new snapshot. - **Epoch change:** remove the old placement state and resynchronize the replica. - **Duplicate event:** ignore it using `(epoch, seq)`. - **Invalid or incomplete snapshot:** do not publish the staging view and retry synchronization. - **Recovery failure:** temporarily fall back to normal load-aware routing. - **Placement-state consumer restart:** fetch a fresh snapshot for every discovered replica, replay events from each replica’s `resume_seq`, and mark each replica as `READY` only after catch-up completes. Recovery stays outside the inference request path and should not block normal request processing. ## Expected Outcome After this change: - a newly started Router can discover KV blocks that already exist; - a restarted placement-state consumer can reconstruct its placement view before resuming cache-aware routing; - short event gaps can be repaired through replay; - gaps outside replay retention can be repaired through a new snapshot; - the parent relationships required by the HashTree can be restored; - multiple TP ranks expose one logical snapshot per KV cache replica; - replica restarts cannot leave stale placement state behind; - cache-aware routing safely degrades to load-aware routing during recovery. ## Related Work This proposal complements the ongoing [external KV Indexer work](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33370) and [event-gap replay work](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32729). It focuses on the missing full-state bootstrap and recovery mechanism.

items.title: [RFC][Simulator] Support Closed-Loop Agentic Workloads
items.body:
## Motivation Completion events and tool waits determine future arrivals in closed-loop workloads, affecting batching, KV-cache reuse and latency. Fixed traces cannot preserve this feedback when simulated inference latency changes. Building on the simulator's serving and replay support (#38423), optional driver coordination would preserve these dependencies while skipping real-time tool waits. ## Design Keep workload semantics in the external driver and add optional time coordination around the existing simulator scheduler. ```mermaid flowchart LR D["Workload driver
Dataset and dependencies
Concurrency, tool timers, benchmark phases"] subgraph SERVER["SGLang simulator"] H["Existing HTTP frontend"] subgraph PROCESS["Scheduler process"] C["Optional coordination
Input barrier and virtual clock
Request terminal events"] S["Existing execution
Scheduling, batching and KV cache
Batch-latency prediction"] end H <-->|Requests / results| S C ---|Scheduler hooks| S end D <-->|HTTP requests / results| H D <-->|Ready / Grant| C ``` The diagram shows `OFFLINE` with a coordinator. Coordination runs inside the scheduler process; it does not introduce a separate service. - **`BLOCKING`:** existing HTTP clients use their own clocks and real tool waits. No coordinator adapter is required. - **`OFFLINE` with a coordinator:** a driver adapter integrates workload transitions and timers so both sides can advance virtual time together. Each dataset or harness implements the same driver contract. Dataset parsing and workflow execution remain outside SGLang; AgentX is one optional integration. ### Coordination HTTP carries model requests and results. A separate loopback ZeroMQ connection carries `Ready/Grant`, with one exchange outstanding. 1. The driver processes current callbacks and due timers, starts HTTP requests, and sends `Ready` with ordered submissions/cancellations and its earliest timer. 2. The simulator waits for every active declared request payload before advancing time. It cannot pass the driver timer. `Grant` reports the reached time and request terminal events. 3. The driver pairs each completion with its HTTP result before releasing dependent work. Other requests remain pending across rounds. A timer can release new requests during a batch. Those requests queue for a later batch; the running batch is not preempted. ### Measurement and completion Coordinated runs use virtual timestamps and native token/cache counts. The driver excludes warmup from measurement while retaining cache state. To stop, the driver sends any required cancellations and declares `finished`. It continues coordination until `FINISHED` confirms that all requests are terminal and native cleanup has drained. ## Initial scope One local driver and scheduler, text requests, ordinary radix cache, and overlap scheduling disabled. Workflows advance on completion or virtual timers. Model-answer quality, real tool execution and explicit sessions are outside scope. See the [driver contract](https://github.com/Jeff010101/sglang/blob/fe1db04aaed893d1614b69c6cc59f85c863ab174/tools/sglang-simulator/README.md#driver-contract) for configuration restrictions and adapter requirements. ## Implementation and validation Draft PR #44287 passed 110 CPU tests on Linux (Python 3.10) without AgentX installed. Its standalone fork/join example preserves virtual timing under 0 and 80 ms HTTP delays with fixed batch costs. This validates coordination, not hardware calibration. Upstream Python 3.12 CI remains pending while the PR is a draft. An optional [AgentX adapter](https://github.com/Jeff010101/agentx-harness/tree/Jeff010101/simulator-runtime) implements the same contract in a separate fork. SGLang does not depend on it.

items.title: [RFC] Context-parallel support for the unified L3 key scheme
items.body:
## Summary

We propose extending `plan_unified_kv` with an explicit ownership rule for each attention-CP mode, so the unified key scheme (#33651) can lift its `attn_cp_size > 1` guard instead of falling back to rank-suffixed keys. Each mode gets a writer rule: replicated CP elects one writer, LayerSplit CP is keyed like a PP stage, and KV cache sharding has each page's owner write the whole page. We would like to agree on the design before sending PRs stacked on #39728.

cc @Shunkangz (unified key scheme, KV cache sharding) @Dovis01 (DSA cache layer split, #29421)

## Motivation

We serve GLM-5.3 (78 layers, DSA) with PD disaggregation on Hopper, using two prefill shapes that should share prefix KV through one Mooncake L3:

| Prefill shape | Parallelism |
| --- | --- |
| DP prefill | DP8 attention, one node |
| LayerSplit prefill | Interleave prefill CP8 with `--enable-dsa-cache-layer-split`; each rank stores about 1/8 of the layers |

Requests move between the two as prompts grow, so a prefix written by one shape is often read by the other. Upstream has no working path for this today:

- **HiCache L3 + LayerSplit does not start.** Mooncake forces the layout away from `layer_first`, while layer-sharded backup only supports `layer_first`. `backup_skip` also lets only `tp_rank == 0` write, which is right for replicated MLA but wrong when each rank owns different layers (details in #37122).
- **The direct linker does not know LayerSplit.** The DSA pool group in `linker_pool_assembler.py` is built over the full `layer_num`.
- **The unified key scheme rejects all CP.** `plan_unified_kv` raises `NotImplementedError` when `attn_cp_size > 1`.

We currently bridge the gap with out-of-tree patches that write per-rank shard keys and reassemble pages across topologies. That works, but each new topology pair needs its own assemble path, which is exactly the coupling the unified scheme removes. We would rather fix this in the scheme.

## Proposal: one ownership rule per CP mode

Today a rank's plan is a layer range × a set of head groups. We add the CP mode as an input; each mode then says which unified-key objects the rank holds completely, so it is their single writer. Keys stay exactly as #39727 defines them; only the writer set changes.

| CP mode | What one rank holds | Who writes each object | What it needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Replicated CP (every rank holds every page and layer, as #30501 describes prefill CP today) | Full pages, all layers | One elected rank, e.g. CP rank 0 | A fixed election rule; no key change |
| LayerSplit CP (`--enable-dsa-cache-layer-split`) | A contiguous layer range, all tokens of each page | Each rank, for its own layer chunks | Chunk-aligned split; the "only the last range may end short" check becomes `end == num_layers` instead of `is_final_stage` |
| KV cache sharding (`--enable-kv-cache-sharding`) | Whole physical pages, all layers | The page's owner (`owner(loc)`) | Writer filter by page owner, in step with #43778's host-page ownership |

The token-sliced CP case named in #39727's error message (ranks holding sub-page slices) stays out of scope here.

Two properties fall out of this. First, LayerSplit is PP from the storage point of view: a contiguous absolute layer range per rank, so the existing `_layer_chunks` logic applies unchanged once the split is chunk-aligned. Second, KV sharding matches on physical pages (per `page_interleave.py`), and each physical page lives on one rank with all its layers, so it writes exactly the objects a DP or TP member writes, on whatever `layer_partition` the fleet uses.

## LayerSplit: a chunk-aligned split

`get_layer_shard_range` gains a chunk size P: it cuts the layers into P-sized chunks and gives each rank a contiguous run of whole chunks. P = 1 reproduces today's split exactly, so the default changes nothing.

The change is required. Today 78 layers over 8 ranks split as 10 × 6 + 9 × 2, so ranges start at 0, 10, …, 60, **69**. `_layer_chunks` requires every start to be a multiple of `layer_partition`, which forces P = 1. With P = 1 every page becomes 78 KV objects of about 41 KiB each, plus one indexer object per indexer layer, multiplying Mooncake master RPCs and metadata by roughly 78× for every fleet member, including DP readers.

With P = 10 the max layers per rank is still 10, so memory is unchanged, and each rank writes exactly one chunk:

| CP rank | Today | P = 10 | Full indexer layers in the chunk | KV object size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | [0, 10) | [0, 10) | 0, 1, 2, 6 | ~410 KiB |
| 1 | [10, 20) | [10, 20) | 10, 14, 18 | ~410 KiB |
| 2 | [20, 30) | [20, 30) | 22, 26 | ~410 KiB |
| 3 | [30, 40) | [30, 40) | 30, 34, 38 | ~410 KiB |
| 4 | [40, 50) | [40, 50) | 42, 46 | ~410 KiB |
| 5 | [50, 60) | [50, 60) | 50, 54, 58 | ~410 KiB |
| 6 | [60, 69) | [60, 70) | 62, 66 | ~410 KiB |
| 7 | [69, 78) | [70, 78) | 70, 74 | ~328 KiB |

Sizes assume 656 B per token per layer (FP8 MLA latent + rope) and page size 64; a whole 78-layer page is ~3.1 MiB. A DP reader on the same grid reads 8 KV objects per page instead of 1. CP4 or CP2 members get whole chunks the same way, so any CP size shares keys with DP, TP and PP members as long as the fleet agrees on P.

Other changes:

1. **PD transfer is unaffected in principle.** Prefill reports `prefill_start_layer` / `prefill_end_layer` per rank and decode pairs on those, not on the split rule. We will still run a PD regression.
2. **Host pool.** LayerSplit backs up one owned layer at a time and only supports `layer_first` today. It needs a `page_unified` per-layer write-back; the load direction already exists (#39726).

## DSA indexer and MTP draft layers

Neither is covered by the #33651 stack yet, and every CP mode needs both.

**Indexer as a second component.** We propose an `_indexer` object at the same coordinate as `_k`: `{page_hash}_{digest}_L{a}-{b}_indexer` next to `{page_hash}_{digest}_L{a}-{b}_k`. Only layers with a real indexer go into it. GLM-5.3 marks 21 of its 78 layers `full` in `indexer_types` (0, 1, 2, then every fourth from 6 to 74); the other 57 are `shared` and already get no host layer (`owned_device_layers` in `pool_host/dsa.py`). So the object for `L{a}-{b}` packs the full layers in `[a, b)` in ascending order, and is skipped when there are none. The indexer layer set is a model fact, so we would add it, or a digest of it, to `KVCacheNamespace` and bump `schema_version`; indexer bytes per token per layer (132 for GLM-5.3) would join the namespace too.

**MTP draft layers.** A draft layer is replicated on every CP rank under LayerSplit; `prefill.py` already sends draft KV from the last CP rank only. We propose a coordinate outside the target model's range, e.g. `D{depth}`, written by the last CP rank under LayerSplit and by the page owner under KV sharding. The GLM-5.2 CP8 LayerSplit recipe in the cookbook runs EAGLE on prefill, so the design should cover it.

## KV cache sharding: no new keys needed

KV sharding needs no new key shape. Allocation and prefix matching use the physical page size, so each L3 page hash covers one physical page, and that page lives on exactly one rank with all its layers. The owner writes the same objects a DP member writes on the fleet's grid (a single `L0-78` object when `layer_partition` is 0), and a DP member reads them back as is.

What it does need sits with the KV sharding work, so we list it rather than propose it:

- **Writer filter.** Only `owner(loc)` backs a page up to L3, instead of `tp_rank == 0`.
- **Prefetch placement.** A page fetched from L3 has to land in a host slot owned by the rank that will hold its device page, which ties prefetch to the rotation-aware allocation in #43778.
- **Lifting the L3 guards** in `kv_shard_hook.py` and #43778 once the two points above hold.

If L3 for KV sharding is planned, the ownership rule above gives it a home, and fleets mixing sharded and unsharded prefill share keys from day one.

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Why not |
| --- | --- |
| Keep LayerSplit's even split and set `layer_partition = 1` | No model-side change, but ~78 KV objects per page for every fleet member, DP readers included |
| Land #37122 as is (rank-suffixed keys under the current scheme) | Fixes LayerSplit-to-LayerSplit reuse only; cross-topology reuse still needs per-pair assemble logic, the coupling #33651 removes |
| Let each rank write chunks clipped to its own range, without aligning the split | A chunk such as `[60, 70)` would span two owners; it would need a cross-rank gather before every write, or partial objects Mooncake does not support |
| Move to KV cache sharding now and skip LayerSplit L3 | Preferable long term, since it needs no layer grid. But DSA under KV sharding currently targets the TRTLLM kernels (#42973), which as far as we know need SM100, and we run Hopper. We would like LayerSplit covered until KV sharding runs GLM DSA on Hopper |

## PR plan, stacked on #39728

1. **CP mode in `plan_unified_kv`**, plus the replicated-CP writer election. Replaces the blanket `attn_cp_size > 1` raise with a per-mode check; the token-sliced mode keeps raising.
2. **Chunk-aligned `get_layer_shard_range`** (default P = 1, no behavior change), then LayerSplit in the key plan: owned global range in, `end == num_layers` for the short tail.
3. **DSA indexer component**: the `_indexer` object, the indexer layer set in `KVCacheNamespace`, and a `schema_version` bump.
4. **`page_unified` per-layer write-back** for layer-sharded DSA host pools, alongside the load kernel from #39726.
5. **End-to-end test**: a LayerSplit CP writer and a DP reader round-trip the same pages byte-exact on a small DSA model.

We will close #37122 with a pointer here once we agree on the direction.

## Open questions

1. Do you agree that LayerSplit CP is a third case, distinct from the two in #39727's error message, and can be keyed like a PP stage?
2. Is changing LayerSplit's split rule acceptable? (@Dovis01)
3. Should the CP mode be an explicit input to `plan_unified_kv`, or derived inside it from the pool type (`LayerSplitDSATokenToKVPool`, the page-interleave pools)?
4. Indexer: a separate `_indexer` object (our proposal), or packed into the `_k` object as a second region?
5. Is a `D{depth}` coordinate for MTP draft layers acceptable, or is there already a plan for draft pools under the unified scheme?
6. Is L3 for KV cache sharding planned? If so, should it build on the same ownership rule, and does the prefetch-placement point match your view?
7. Order: wait for #39728 to merge, or open the first PR against it now?

Related: #21846 (roadmap), #33651, #39727, #39728, #39815, #30501, #43778, #42973, #29421, #37122.

items.title: [HiCache] Add L2 prefetch-buffer-only memory mode
items.body:
## Motivation

Now in HiCache each worker allocates a large exclusive host memory pool (up to hundreds of gb per 1GPU worker).
Popular prefixes get duplicated in every worker's host cache, wasting the majority of the memory budget. Meanwhile, the shared storage backend (MoonCake) is allocated a relatively small pool and remains underutilized.
With `buffer_only` mode, host memory shrinks to a tiny staging buffer (up to dozens gb per worker), and the freed budget goes entirely to the shared storage pool. Any worker can read data written by any other worker, eliminating duplication.

## Modifications

1. New `buffer_only` host memory mode: host memory acts as a small transient staging buffer instead of a persistent cache tier. Pages are freed immediately after the async storage write completes. Controlled via `--hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only` and `--hicache-buffer-pages`.
2. `storage_backed` flag on TreeNode: tracks whether a node is durably written to external storage, allowing GPU eviction without losing the node from the radix tree. Unified with `backuped` via new `storage_ready` property.
3. Pending write queue: handles backpressure when the small host buffer is full, nodes wait in a queue and drain each scheduler step.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3/Qwen3-32B-FP8

```
python benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 500 --num-shots 48 --parallel 100
```

With hot cache in MoonCake:

L2 as cache mode:
```
Accuracy: 0.934
Invalid: 0.000
Latency: 68.659 s
Output throughput: 870.155 token/s
```

L2 as buffer only:
```
Accuracy: 0.936
Invalid: 0.000
Latency: 67.984 s
Output throughput: 876.645 token/s
```

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Qwen3-32B-FP8 on 8xH200 with TP1.
Common flags:
```
--mem-fraction-static 0.8 --page-size 64 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-running-requests 64 --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-mem-layout page_first_direct --hicache-storage-prefetch-policy wait_complete
```

Configuration for `buffer_only`:
* `--hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only --hicache-buffer-pages 512`
* MoonCake: 1024 gb on the same node

Configuration for `cache`:
* `--hicache-host-memory-mode cache --hicache-ratio 2.0` (107 gb host memory per worker)
* MoonCake: 224 gb on the same node
* Total: 1080 gb

MoonCake Traces bench with `toolagent` workload and 0.5 slowdown factor.

| Metric | `buffer_only`  | `cache` | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cache hit rate | 45.9% | 38.7% | +7.2% |
| Storage hits | 6.08M tokens | 1.53M tokens | 4.0x |
| GPU hits | 19.0M tokens | 18.9M tokens |  |
| E2E P99 | 29,910 ms | 31,468 ms | −5% |
| TTFT P99 | 3,526 ms | 3,996 ms | −12% |
| TPOT P99 | 432 ms | 492 ms | −12% |
| ITL P99 | 181 ms | 206 ms | −12% |

items.title: feat: add kv hint envelope to request transport
items.body:
## Motivation                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 A KV hint is advisory routing metadata attached by a trusted orchestrator (a router or a scheduler) after it has picked a worker -- never by an application client. A KV-aware router already knows which worker holds a prefix; today there is no way for it to tell the worker it just picked. This adds the transport for that, and nothing else.                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
This is the transport-only half of #36224, split out on review feedback so the KVCR backend that consumes a hint lands as a purely additive follow-up.                        
                                                                                            
## Modifications                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
The envelope travels unchanged from the entrypoint down to the scheduler's `Req`, and nothing in the core reads a payload:                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                              
  GenerateReqInput (HTTP/Engine) and the gRPC KVHintsEnvelope message                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
    -> normalization (single, per-batch-item, and parallel-sample expansion)                                                                                                            
    -> TokenizedGenerateReqInput over msgpack IPC                                                                                                                                                                        
    -> Req                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                     
 The envelope is a list of independent actions, each naming its own type and version, so a consumer implementing one action type ignores -- rather than rejects -- an action it                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
    -> normalization (single, per-batch-item, and parallel-sample expansion)                                                                                                            
    -> TokenizedGenerateReqInput over msgpack IPC                           
    -> Req                                    

The envelope is a list of independent actions, each naming its own type and version, so a consumer implementing one action type ignores -- rather than rejects -- an action it does not implement sitting next to it. The payload is therefore untyped here; the component that implements an action owns its schema and validates it. **No action types are defined by this change.**

 New module `python/sglang/srt/managers/kv_hints.py` holds the `KvHintAction` / `KvHintsEnvelope` msgspec structs and `decode_kv_hints_envelope()`.

 Wire-compatible with vLLM's `KVHintsEnvelope` (vllm-project/vllm#53423) so one orchestrator can address either engine with the same envelope.

 ## Accuracy Test

  No model behavior changes -- an absent or malformed envelope leaves the request on the existing path.

 ## Benchmarking and Profiling

 No hot-path change; the field is `None` for every request that does not carry a hint.

  ## Checklist

  - [x] Format your code according to the Code Formatting with Pre-Commit.
  - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py`, covering normalization, batch expansion, parallel-sample expansion, and rejection of a malformed envelope).
  - [x] Update documentation as needed.

items.title: feat: first-class session identity in SGLang
items.body:
Adds a scalar top-level `session_id` as stable request identity and wires it through native, Engine, OpenAI, Responses, and gRPC entry points. This keeps continual-prompt `session_params` unchanged while letting the existing session radix cache use `session_id` without requiring `/open_session`.

### How This Was Implemented

- Keep `session_params` on the existing opened `SessionController` path.
- Use top-level `session_id` as the sole identity for radix-session tagging when `--enable-session-radix-cache` is enabled.
- Keep cache policy gated in the cache, so carrying identity alone does not activate session-radix behavior.
- Separate radix release from the legacy/streaming `release_session` hook.

<details>
<summary>Walkthrough</summary>

- Request adapters pass the scalar `session_id` through tokenization into `Req`.
- The scheduler routes `session_params` and `session_id` independently and rejects native requests that set both.
- Radix sessions begin implicitly on first use and release tagged KV through `/close_session`; legacy sessions retain `/open_session` semantics.

</details>

### Validation

- `247 passed, 25 subtests passed` across request normalization, OpenAI adapters, session caches, and server arguments.
- Rust gRPC request mapping test passes.
- Repository pre-commit checks and protobuf validation pass.
- Live Llama 3.2 1B: radix sessions worked without open, reused 11 cached tokens, and reclaimed tagged KV on close.
- On the same flag-enabled server, `/open_session` plus `session_params` continued through `SessionController` and closed independently.

items.title: feat: Session-reference-aware Unified Radix Cache for agentic multi-turn workloads
items.body:
## Motivation In multi-turn inference workloads such as agentic workflows and RL rollouts, active sessions accumulate reusable KV prefixes across turns. Under memory pressure, the standard radix cache evicts entries using only the configured cache policy, without considering whether a prefix is still referenced by an active session. This may evict an active session's prefix while unrelated, unreferenced KV remains cached, causing unnecessary recomputation in later turns and reducing cache hit rate and throughput. ## Design This PR adds session-aware eviction to `UnifiedRadixCache`. Applications pass a stable top-level `session_id` with each request. When a request finishes, SGLang registers its reusable KV under that session. When the session ends, the application calls `/close_session` to release those references. ```text --enable-session-radix-cache | +------------------+------------------+ | | request finished session closed | | register_session_ref(req) release_radix_session(id) | | +------------- session refs ----------+ | UnifiedRadixCache | +------------------+------------------+ | | | FULL SWA MAMBA reusable prefix path sliding window reusable state leaf | | | +------------------+------------------+ | device and host eviction | UNREFERENCED -> REFERENCED ``` Each UnifiedRadixCache component tracks the KV region reusable by a session: - **FULL attention** tracks the reusable prefix path. Eviction orders nodes by `(is_referenced, session_ref_count, base_eviction_priority)`. - **SWA** tracks the reusable sliding-window tail. Device and host eviction use two LRU passes: unreferenced nodes first, then referenced nodes if more space is required. - **Mamba** tracks the reusable state at the session frontier. It uses the same two-pass unreferenced-first fallback. Referenced KV is soft-protected, not pinned. If unreferenced KV is insufficient, referenced entries remain evictable. Closing a session removes its references without immediately freeing its KV, allowing the KV to remain reusable until normal eviction reclaims it. Session generations and bounded closed-session tombstones prevent stale in-flight requests from reattaching references after close or close/reopen. This feature is implemented only by `UnifiedRadixCache`. Ordinary `RadixCache` and `HiRadixCache` do not maintain session references. Storage-backed L3 cache is not included in this PR. ## Modifications - Add `SessionUnifiedRadixCacheMixin` for session lifecycle and stale-request protection. - Add per-component session leaf indexes and compact reference counts for FULL, SWA, and Mamba. - Apply session-aware ordering to both device and host eviction. - Register reusable KV when requests finish and release references through `/close_session`. - Support top-level `session_id` without changing or reconstructing request prompts. - Preserve the configured base eviction policy without requiring `--radix-eviction-policy priority`. - Remove session tracking and `SessionAwareEvictionStrategy` integration from ordinary `RadixCache` and `HiRadixCache`. - Add focused tests for UnifiedRadixCache ownership, registration, release, stale generations, and unreferenced-first eviction. - Add documentation for enablement, request lifecycle, and per-component eviction behavior. - Enable the feature with `--enable-session-radix-cache`; `UnifiedRadixCache` must also be enabled. ## Speed Tests and Profiling We evaluate session radix cache on a SWE-agent agentic workload using GLM-5.2 (UnifiedRadixCache) under different batch sizes. The cache hit rate breakdown between the original HiCache and session radix cache is shown below.

The results show that session-reference-aware radix cache substantially improves both cache hit rate and end-to-end throughput. By preserving KV cache entries that are still referenced by active multi-turn requests, session radix cache reduces unnecessary prefix recomputation and improves cache residency under memory pressure. However, we also observe that the cache hit rate still drops at larger batch sizes. This suggests that large batches can still cause KV cache thrashing, even with reference-aware eviction. Addressing this issue may require additional mechanisms such as cache-aware admission control, batch throttling, or concurrency control, similar to the approaches explored in ThunderAgent and Concur. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #30707949357](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30707949357) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #30707949287](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30707949287)

items.title: [mem_cache] soft retention: priority decay via retention_seconds
items.body:
## Summary

Adds **soft retention** to the priority eviction policy: a request may attach
`retention_seconds` alongside `priority`; under `--radix-eviction-policy
priority`, the node's effective priority decays to 0 once idle time since
last access exceeds the retention duration. This is the engine-side
Retain/Pin primitive named in RFC #27574, carrying forward the design from
#21045 (@ishandhanani), rebased onto current main.

## Design

- **Lazy decay, no machinery**: decay is evaluated inside
  `PriorityStrategy.get_priority()` at eviction time by comparing
  `last_access_time + retention_duration` to now. No background threads, no
  expiry heap, no pinned slots.
- **The pool can never be wedged**: retained KV stays ordinary evictable
  radix. Under enough pressure it is evicted and re-prefilled — protection is
  a bias, not a lock (contrast with the reverted hard TTL pin #18941/#21884
  and the streaming-session pinning issues #27024/#27025).
- **Refresh-on-hit**: cache hits update `last_access_time`, so live sessions
  auto-extend their window (Continuum-style).
- **Coherent shared prefixes**: `pick_stronger_policy` keeps shared-prefix
  nodes on one (priority, retention) tuple — higher priority wins; on equal
  priority, longer retention wins, with 0/None = permanent dominating.
- **Priority clamped to [0, 99]** (100 discrete levels), mirroring TRT-LLM's
  `TokenRangeRetentionConfig` (`retention_priority` 0-100 + `duration_ms`),
  and preparing for an O(1) bucket-queue optimization later.
- **Plumbing**: `GenerateReqInput` -> `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` -> `Req` ->
  `InsertParams.retention_duration` -> `TreeNode`, in both `RadixCache` and
  `HiRadixCache` insert paths; node splits inherit. OpenAI chat/completions
  forward `retention_seconds` exactly like `priority` (settable via
  `extra_body`).
- **Default off**: without `retention_seconds`, behavior is byte-identical
  under every eviction policy.

## Evidence (A100-80G, Qwen2.5-7B, agentic-session workload from #27969)

Agent sessions (priority 50, retention 30s, 12k-token scaffolds, tool gaps)
vs priority-0 bulk traffic on a constrained pool, LRU vs priority+retention:

| | LRU | retention |
|---|---:|---:|
| turn-0 p95 TTFT (cold-prefill control) | 7053ms | 6966ms |
| **continuation-turn p95 TTFT** | **2732ms** | **1095ms (2.5x)** |
| continuation-turn mean TTFT | 1263ms | 903ms |

Honest scoping from the same study: when the protected working set itself
oversubscribes the pool, or in-flight KV crowds out everything evictable,
retention (correctly) cannot help — equal-priority ties degrade to LRU order.

## Tests

- `test_evict_policy.py`: clamping, decay-at-expiry, active-retention,
  zero-retention-is-permanent, `pick_stronger_policy` coherence (9 new tests;
  file total 32 green).
- `test_radix_cache_unit.py`: integration test — a shared prefix inheriting
  (99, 1s) from a stronger leaf is evicted before an unexpired (60, 300s)
  node once expired (mocked clock; deterministic).
- Both registered in existing CPU CI suites.

---

*Disclosure: developed with AI assistance (Claude Fable 5). All benchmark
numbers are from real GPU runs; raw data available.*

items.title: Add experimental agent-aware KV cache hints
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the first experimental slice of agent-aware KV cache support.

Changes include:

- Add optional `agent_hints` request metadata for OpenAI-compatible chat and completion requests.
- Propagate `agent_hints` through request normalization, tokenizer manager, scheduler request construction, and session request handling.
- Annotate radix-cache nodes with optional agent metadata such as workflow ID, agent ID, step ID, parent step ID, TTL, expected tool duration, and reuse hint.
- Add an experimental `agent_aware` radix eviction policy.
- Add unit coverage for protocol parsing, request normalization, radix metadata annotation, and eviction priority behavior.

## Motivation

Agentic workloads often issue multi-step requests where KV reuse value depends on workflow context, expected tool latency, and future reuse likelihood.

This PR keeps the implementation intentionally narrow:

- Existing behavior is unchanged by default.
- `agent_hints` is optional metadata.
- The new eviction behavior is only used when the experimental `agent_aware` policy is selected.
- TTL and reuse hints are soft eviction-ranking signals, not hard pinning.

References
[SGLang / RadixAttention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07104): motivates KV-cache reuse for structured, multi-call language model programs. This PR builds on that idea by attaching optional workflow metadata to radix-cache nodes.
[PagedAttention / vLLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180): shows that KV-cache memory management is a core bottleneck in LLM serving. This PR adds a small policy hook for metadata-aware cache eviction.
[KVFlow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07400): directly motivates workflow-aware KV-cache management for multi-agent workloads, where LRU can evict entries shortly before reuse. This PR implements only a narrow metadata and eviction-ranking subset of that idea.
[Mooncake](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00079): treats KV cache as a first-class serving resource. This PR follows the same high-level direction, but does not implement distributed KV-cache scheduling or transfer.
[LMCache](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09665): motivates explicit KV-cache reuse across engines and queries. This PR does not add a KV-cache API, but prepares a small metadata path useful for future cache-control work.

## Scope

This PR does not implement:

- Programmatic KV cache APIs
- Router changes
- Distributed cache migration
- HiCache / Mooncake / NIXL integration
- Hard cache pinning
- Cross-worker KV movement
- Shared-prefix routing

Those are larger follow-up areas.

## Tests

Ran targeted tests:

```text
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py -k agent
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_evict_policy.py -k agent
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_protocol.py -k agent
python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py -k agent
```
Also ran compile checks on touched Python files.

items.title: feat(hicache): retain hinted prompt KV in Mooncake L3
items.body:
<!-- codex-pr-description:start -->
This draft adds a provider-neutral `kv_hints` request envelope and applies full-prompt retention to committed HiCache pages in Mooncake L3. It lets Dynamo request bounded prompt-KV survival without pinning GPU/host cache or moving routing, scheduling, and eviction policy out of SGLang.

CLOSES: DYN-3309

Companion PRs: [Dynamo #11534](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/11534) and [Mooncake #2835](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/2835). The cross-layer design is tracked in [SGLang RFC #27574](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/27574).

### How This Was Implemented
- Added `KvHintEnvelope { retain_full_prompt }` to engine, tokenizer-manager, scheduler, session, and disaggregated request plumbing with a cross-language JSON fixture.
- Resolves the page-aligned full prompt against committed HiRadix nodes and uses their exact tagged Mooncake page hashes.
- Reuses HiCache's storage-worker queue so Mooncake metadata I/O never blocks the scheduler thread.
- Requires HiCache `write_through`, Mooncake group semantics, and `retain_groups`; unsupported configurations warn once and inference continues.
- Bounds each request to 8,192 unique pages and a 24-hour TTL by default, with backend-extra-config overrides.

<details>
<summary>Walkthrough</summary>

#### Mental model

The hint expresses retention intent only. SGLang remains responsible for radix insertion and page identity, while Mooncake owns the L3 lease and eviction protection.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Engine request + KvHintEnvelope"] --> B["Tokenizer manager and scheduler Req"]
    B --> C["Normal HiRadix insertion"]
    C --> D["Resolve committed page hashes"]
    D --> E["Queue RetentionOperation"]
    E --> F["HiCache storage worker"]
    F --> G["Mooncake retain_groups(group_ids, ttl)"]
```

#### State and ordering

Retention is attempted only after ordinary unfinished or finished radix insertion. The full prompt is rounded down to the HiCache page size, matched back to a single committed prefix, and converted to the page hashes already used by Mooncake group publication.

Each request tracks the pages and maximum TTL already applied, so unfinished/final cache events do not repeatedly renew the same lease. Nested/shared pages are deduplicated and a later shorter TTL cannot reduce an earlier request-local TTL.

#### Request lifecycle

1. `GenerateReqInput` validates and normalizes the provider-neutral envelope, including batch and parallel-sampling expansion.
2. The hint survives tokenizer IPC, disaggregated encode/decode plumbing, and session request construction.
3. After radix insertion, `HiRadixCache.apply_kv_hints` verifies that the complete page-aligned prompt is committed.
4. A `RetentionOperation` enters the existing storage backup queue; the storage worker calls Mooncake `retain_groups` asynchronously.
5. Missing capability, partial acceptance, or Mooncake failure affects retention only; generation remains fail-open and logs the outcome.

#### Boundaries and limitations

- This retains L3 objects only. GPU L1 and host L2 remain normally evictable.
- Only classic HiRadix + Mooncake `write_through` is supported; Unified/Hybrid/Mamba caches warn and ignore the hint.
- There is no prefetch, demote, share, release, routing, or scheduler-priority behavior in this PR.
- Bounds are per request, not a global byte-aware or tenant-fair retention budget.
- A Mooncake release containing `retain_groups` is required before this can leave draft.

</details>

### Validation
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_retention_hints.py test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_group_semantics.py` — 43 passed.
- `pre-commit run ruff --files <changed Python files>` — passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Two-worker MiniMax M2.7 TP4 H100 validation through Dynamo, real Codex, real Claude Code, Mooncake, compressed `DYN_REQUEST_TRACE`, and Tachometer — passed functional retention attribution.

### Benchmark Results

The final A/B seeded each client on one worker, drove Mooncake eviction with 70 × 16,384-token pressure requests, flushed both workers' local caches, then resumed each session on the other worker. Every final probe had `router_cached=0`, isolating request-time Mooncake restoration.

| Probe | Control L3 tokens | Retained L3 tokens | Retention TTL | Probe latency delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Codex | 4,640 shared-prefix tokens | 20,800 tokens | 30 minutes | +23.1% |
| Claude Code | 0 tokens | 13,600 tokens | 1 hour | +34.0% |

| Pressure outcome | Result |
|---|---:|
| Completed pressure requests | 70 |
| Total pressure input | 1,146,881 tokens |
| Mooncake eviction | 144,904 keys / 34.27 GiB |
| Mooncake accepted retained groups | Codex 1,300/1,300; Claude 850/850 |

The mechanism survived eviction, but it is not yet a latency win on this single-node H100 topology: Mooncake materialization was slower than recomputing these prefixes. This PR should remain a draft until the dependency and L3 materialization-cost follow-ups are resolved.
<!-- codex-pr-description:end -->
