items.title: [Radix Cache] Add Rust TreeCore backend with shared parity tests
items.body:
## Motivation

Add an in-tree Rust implementation of `UnifiedTreeCoreInterface` for Unified Radix Cache while retaining Python cache orchestration, pools, and action application. The same cache-level unit suite now exercises both Python and Rust TreeCore implementations, exposing parity gaps through shared assertions rather than backend-specific test copies.

## What changed

- Added the standalone `rust/mem-cache` core, PyO3 bindings, and Python adapter/registry integration.
- Added a test-only `UnifiedTreeCoreInspectionInterface` and Python/Rust inspectors.
  - Inspection returns owned snapshots; no Python iterator crosses the Rust boundary.
  - Production bindings are inspection-free and carry no inspector-only per-node state.
- Added NVIDIA CI entry points for the shared UnifiedRadixCache suite and benchmark/fuzz suite with both backends, plus native Rust and adapter tests on CPU.
- Ported intervening cache behavior as separate commits:
  - #33091: allocation-aware one-mutation eviction steps
  - #36317: Full-only write-back load ownership
  - #31479: KV-event coalescing
  - #31902: unsafe prefetch-refill rejection
  - #33639: incremental Mamba backup
  - #34808: DCP-aware Mamba checkpoint grid
  - #32228: partial lock skip/replay
  - #36637: Full-only frees during SWA tombstone recovery
  - #2571/#29901: DFS-weight scheduling through handles
  - #26227/#29901: PD-decode HiCache through handles
  - #34798/#35769: buffer-only backup intents and load ownership
  - #30827: cache-salt `KeyNamespace` isolation and salt-aware KV events
  - #36382: request-namespaced buffer prefetch
  - #36834: live buffer-prefetch anchor rematching and staged-span trimming
  - #37091: adopted insert-range reporting; external linker execution remains deferred
- Added typed boundary errors, stale-handle checks, poisoned-core fail-closed behavior, authoritative Rust configuration, and input validation.
- Synced Mamba request-state access with #37164 and serialized shared Cargo-target mutations across concurrent Base/Extra extension builds and source-build fallback.
- Packaged the production extension with fingerprinted loading, kept inspection bindings isolated, and added native mem-cache/release-wheel CI coverage.

## Supported scope

- Full, Full+SWA, Full+Mamba, and Full+SWA+Mamba TreeCore configurations.
- Standard and EAGLE/bigram radix keys.
- Cache-mode HiCache and buffer-only HiCache for Full/Full+SWA.
- Cache-salt namespace isolation, split/prefetch propagation, and salt-aware KV-event hashes.
- DFS-weight scheduling and PD-decode HiCache without Python node-object traversal.
- Runtime storage attach/detach and existing L3/KV-event flows.

## Explicitly unsupported / deferred

These combinations fail early instead of silently running with incomplete semantics:

- Session radix cache and session-reference-aware eviction (#29173). Rust shared tests omit only the session-enabled subcases until this is ported.
- Python `component_registry_override` implementations and C128 (#25754/#33676). C128 remains outside the current NVIDIA scope.
- External cache linker (#37091/#37151). Rust preserves adopted insert ranges but does not yet implement linker persistence and transfer semantics; enabling it is explicitly rejected with a `TODO(Jialin)` follow-up.
- Direct Python `node_by_id` / `root_node` object access. Supported production consumers use backend-neutral handles/scalar APIs; remaining object consumers belong to the deferred session/custom-component paths.
- Production deployment on AMD, MLX, or NPU. This PR validates NVIDIA production use and CPU Rust unit/binding coverage. CUDA 13.4 / PyTorch 2.15 is also not enabled; packaged Rust TreeCore currently targets the validated PyTorch 2.11–2.13 range.

## Verification

- Shared UnifiedRadixCache suite: 2,436 cases pass with each backend.
- Generated fixture-backed matrix: 2,356 cases across 19 Full/SWA/Mamba configurations route through the selected inspector.
- Native Rust suite: 831 passed, 1 ignored.
- Rust adapter/integration suite: 100 passed.
- Python and Rust benchmark/fuzz suites: 15 passed each.
- Production/inspection isolation: production exposes no `inspect_*` methods; the separate inspection module exposes the shared test surface and is excluded from wheels.
- Full changed-file pre-commit suite, Rust clippy with warnings denied, rustfmt, CI registry validation, and wheel/import smoke tests pass.

## Review notes

The parity review covered result/action mapping, eviction and load-back semantics, HiCache ownership, namespace/event hashing, stale handles and panic boundaries, mutable configuration, FFI allocation hot spots, extension freshness/packaging, CI discovery, and shared-suite routing. Remaining feature gaps are fenced above and have nearby `TODO(Jialin)` references.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers.
3. Trigger the required CI suites.

items.title: [Rust TreeCore] Support external cache linker
items.body:
## Motivation

The unified external-cache linker already supports the Python TreeCore, but its wrapper still traverses and mutates Python `UnifiedTreeNode` objects directly. The Rust TreeCore intentionally exposes opaque `NodeId` handles instead of Python node proxies, so the existing linker cannot run with it.

Replace those object-level dependencies with backend-neutral TreeCore operations and port the existing Full and Full+SWA linker state machine to Rust.

This PR is based directly on `main` after the merged #37290 crate rename. It is independent of #37303 and of the Mooncake transport integration in #37205.

## Modifications

- Add backend-neutral TreeCore operations to:
  - build external offload transfer snapshots;
  - mark successfully restored paths as externally stored;
  - publish accepted offloads as pending;
  - finish or roll back offloads across split fragments.
- Refactor `UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper` to use those operations instead of resolving raw Python tree nodes.
- Add the corresponding Rust TreeCore state and behavior:
  - hash nodes while the linker is enabled;
  - trigger offload only for nodes not already stored externally;
  - stop backup chains at externally stored ancestors;
  - preserve external stored and pending state across node splits;
  - build Full and trailing-window SWA offload transfers.
- Validate linker `NodeId` inputs through the existing fallible TreeCore boundary and map stale handles to Python `KeyError`.
- Keep Mamba and custom components explicitly unsupported; the Python external linker does not support Mamba transfers either.
- Normalize EAGLE keys before external lookup hashing so Python and Rust use the same bigram hash chain.
- Add shared backend-routed coverage for Full, Full+SWA, EAGLE, split/failure/retry, deduplication, and reset/lock cleanup.

## Known Limitations

This parity port intentionally preserves existing Python external-linker behavior:

- external-linker keys are not namespace-aware, so `cache_salt` must not be combined with the linker until both offload and lookup use a salted hash chain;
- canceled or failed external loads do not yet roll back published tree allocations;
- independently queued ancestor/descendant offloads can still require a retry if the ancestor fails after the descendant succeeds.

These are shared linker follow-ups, not Rust-specific differences introduced here.

## Accuracy Tests

No model kernels or numerical computation are changed.

Validation on the independent branch:

- Rust native suite: 837 passed, 1 ignored.
- External-linker unit tests: 16 passed.
- Rust all-target compile with the Python extension enabled: passed.
- Rust formatting and repository diff checks: passed.

The broader CUDA backend matrix and CI verification will be run separately.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No benchmark was run. The new behavior is gated behind external-linker enablement; transfer construction occurs on the external I/O path, and tensors remain shallow views across the Rust/Python boundary.

## Checklist

items.title: [Unified Cache][5/N]: Integrate external linker mode end to end
items.body:
## Motivation

Motivation
Unified Radix Cache manages heterogeneous model states, including full-attention KV, SWA KV, and model-specific sidecars.

On GB platforms, deployments may need to aggregate larger memory regions into a shared Global Memory pool. This requires an efficient way for Unified Radix Cache to access remote memory directly without overhead on the inference critical path.

This PR adds an optional external-cache linker mode. It allows the tree to access a Global Memory pool through backends such as Mooncake or UMBP .. while retaining ownership of allocation, insertion, component consistency, and cache-node lifetime.

The existing hierarchical cache path remains unchanged. The linker is an opt-in alternative for deployments that need a larger shared memory pool while preserving inference performance.

This is the fifth PR split from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35687. It completes the Mooncake external-linker path.

Previous splits: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37091, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37098, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37151, and https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37205.

items.title: [Feat] unified_cache: Support hybrid SWA + Mamba models in the Mooncake direct linker
items.body:
## Motivation

The unified-cache external linker (direct L3, no host tier) supports Full and SWA tree components only. Hybrid SWA + Mamba models such as Inkling are rejected at startup by both the Python wrapper and the Rust tree core, and the Mamba component's linker hooks raise.

Depends on #44220: Inkling replays the Full prefill CUDA graph by default, and without #44220 a loading batch can replay before its layer-wise load lands.

## Modifications

**Device pool group for FULL + SWA + MAMBA** (`linker_pool_assembler.py`, `hybrid_pool_assembler.py`)
- `_MambaSwaStrategy.build_direct_linker_pool_group`: the full-attention and SWA MHA pools each pack a layer's K and V into one page object; the Mamba pool is slot-addressed (one row per state slot; the empty temporal state of conv-only models is skipped).
- Rejected at startup with a clear error: `--enable-unified-memory`, int8 Mamba checkpoints, Mamba side states (short conv / ngram), and scaled KV caches.

**Mamba component** (`components/mamba.py`)
- OFFLOAD: one state per checkpoint node, keyed by the node's last page hash under `TRAILING_PAGES`, so a prefix is restorable only where a stored state ends.
- LOOKUP / LOAD: the state of the restorable prefix's last page. LOAD allocates the slot the state is loaded into (`_alloc_mamba_slot`, evicting if needed, same sizing contract as HiCache's `prepare_load_back`).
- PREPARE binds the loaded slot as the request's own state (freeing a slot it already held, e.g. from a shorter device CoW match) and drops the deferred CoW/clear and the ReplaySSM cursor, shared with the HiCache buffer load-back via `_adopt_loaded_state`. The forward then reads the state layer by layer through the linker's layer counter, already registered on `req_to_token_pool` for Mamba pools. ABORT frees the loaded slot.

**Wrapper** (`unified_cache_linker.py`)
- Accept `ComponentType.MAMBA`.

**Mooncake keys** (`mooncake_store.py`)
- A linker `DevicePoolEntry` always maps to one object per page per pool (`_k` for KV, `_{pool}` otherwise); the layer-wise load reads one key per location. Without this, the MHA SWA entry has no key scheme (`Unsupported Mooncake hybrid pool name: swa`). Keys for the existing DeepSeek-V4 / DSA linker pools are unchanged: those groups are rank-replicated and already took the single-object branch.

**Rust tree core**
- Drop the Mamba rejection in `set_enable_external_cache_linker` and add `MambaComponent::build_external_linker_offload_transfer` (without it the Rust core never offloads a Mamba state, so it never restores one).

## Tests

- `test_unified_cache_linker.py` (Python and Rust tree cores): `test_mamba_state_round_trips_only_at_its_checkpoint` (offload keys, restorable only at a stored state, LOAD/PREPARE binding, insert), `test_mamba_load_supersedes_a_shorter_device_cow` (a shorter device CoW must not overwrite the loaded state or leak its slot).
- `test_linker_pool_assembler.py::test_mamba_swa_uses_hybrid_assembler_strategy`: K/V packing offsets, slot-addressed Mamba rows, empty temporal state skipped.
- Linker, pool-assembler and Mooncake unit tests: 89 passed; `cargo test --lib`: 930 passed.

## Accuracy Tests

**Temporary CI skip:** `test_unified_cache_linker_kl_inkling.py` is disabled in CI until #44220 is merged and included in the tested branch (tracking deadline: 2026-10-29). Re-enable its CI registration after that fix lands. This lets dependent PRs proceed, but does not remove the runtime correctness dependency on #44220: Full prefill graph replay can read incomplete layer-wise loads without it. The measured results below are unchanged.

New `test_unified_cache_linker_kl_inkling.py` (tiny `thinkingmachines/Inkling --revision test`, Mooncake, `--enable-deterministic-inference`, default Full prefill CUDA graph). This checkpoint scores every token identically in prefill and decode, so the threshold is a 1e-9 floor, not a tolerance. Turn 1 offloads, `/flush_cache` drops the device tree, turn 2 restores from Mooncake alone (asserts `cached_tokens_details.host == cached_tokens`) and is replayed against recomputed logprobs.

Measured on 1x GB300 (Mooncake over TCP), with #44220 applied:

| Run | avg KL |
|---|---|
| This PR, 4 runs (one at the current head) | 0.0 each |
| This PR, 0.2 s injected delay per loaded layer | 0.0 |
| Without #44220 | 2.5e-3 (fails) |
| Linker disabled (cold recompute, oracle check) | 0.0 |
| Negative control: loaded Mamba state cleared before the forward | 8.0e-5 (fails) |

## Known limitations

- Not covered: FULL + Mamba without SWA, the UMBP (mori) backend, unified memory, scaled KV, int8 Mamba checkpoints, Mamba side states.
- A Mamba checkpoint attached to a node that is already stored externally (e.g. a split / branching point) is not offloaded again; this loses a hit but does not affect correctness.

Related: #39511 (FULL + Mamba on UMBP for Kimi K3); the pool group, UMBP and DCP parts there are complementary to this PR.

- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy evaluation results.

items.title: [HiCache] Add the page_unified host KV layout and the unified L3 key
items.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Two halves of one proposal: a host page layout whose axis order makes an L3 chunk a single byte run, and a key scheme that names those chunks without naming who wrote them. Library only -- no server arg and no transfer arm yet, so nothing here is reachable from the CLI; the integration PR adds both at once rather than shipping a flag that does nothing.

The layout, page_unified:

```
  MHA: (page, head_group, layer, 2, page_size, head_in_group, dim)   K=0, V=1
  MLA: (page, layer, page_size, dim)
```

matching the write-back kernel in #39606 and the load-back kernel this stack already landed, so a page is byte-identical whether it arrived from the device or from L3.

A PARTITION AXIS MUST BE OUTER. The grid cuts a page along the kv-head axis and then along the layer axis, so both sit outside page_size and a chunk becomes an offset and a length. The K/V axis sits INSIDE the layer axis rather than outside the pool, which is what lets one object carry both components: hoisting it out -- as layer_first and page_first_direct do -- makes a chunk two objects whose runs interleave at token granularity. The result is that every chunk is exactly one run, a ragged final layer window included, so the transport never has to switch descriptor forms mid-plan.

The key scheme replaces the rank suffixes (_{tp_rank}_{tp_size}, _{pp_size}_{pp_rank}, _cp{r}_{s}) with

```
  {page_hash}_{digest}_L{start}-{end}[_H{head_group}]
```

The coordinate names what an object holds -- a layer-range x head-range rectangle of one page, K and V together -- so a TP2 rank's objects are exactly the union of two TP4 ranks', and a PP1 rank's the union of the stages'. Both union properties are tested, because nothing else in the stack checks them and the failure mode is a silent 0% hit rate rather than an error.

head_group and layer_partition are fleet-wide agreements, not local tuning: they fix chunk boundaries, and the boundaries are namespace identity. Unset, each falls back to this rank's own shard and shares only with its own topology; the head case logs a warning, since the symptom is again a silent miss.

head_group_num is a constructor argument on MHATokenToKVPoolHost because it sizes the buffer. Under page_unified, k_buffer and v_buffer raise: the components are interleaved inside a page block, so kv_buffer[0] is a page there, not the K half-pool.

Tested: 23 CPU unit cases. The layout side pins that the declared strides equal the allocated tensor's, that chunks tile a page exactly once with no gap or overlap, that a 61-layer/30-partition tail is still one run, and that the head-group count permutes a page without resizing it. The key side pins the two union properties, that every identity field reaches the digest (a field that does not would let different bytes collide on one key), and each rejection. Separately smoke-tested on B200 that the pools allocate the declared shapes for head_group_num in {1, 2, 8} and for MLA.

items.title: [Feat] scheduler: Overlap prefill scheduling and KV loading with model execution
items.body:
**Implementation status:** runtime integration, CPU regression checks, and initial PD experiments have been performed locally against main base `92580581da`. The implementation has not been pushed: this Draft PR still has an intentionally empty diff. Supporting authoring files remain local. Further validation and performance investigation are in progress; this is not ready for merge. **Design RFC:** https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44721 ## Motivation **Native overlap can leave only A's GPU tail to hide the next batch's preparation.** The scheduler regains control after the synchronous CPU model call returns. During prefill, layer traversal, input preparation, kernel launches, and communication submission can occupy much of that call. Retiring C, preparing B, and discovering B's cached-KV load can therefore happen late. **V2 moves that preparation into A's CPU model-call window.** One persistent forward worker runs A's model call while the scheduler retires independent C results, receives ready requests, prepares B, and starts its KV loading earlier. A = current batch, B = next batch, C = an earlier batch. ```mermaid %%{init: {"theme": "base", "gantt": {"displayMode": "compact", "barHeight": 30, "barGap": 8, "fontSize": 13, "sectionFontSize": 14, "leftPadding": 190, "rightPadding": 45}, "themeVariables": {"taskBkgColor": "#dff2e8", "taskBorderColor": "#318463", "taskTextColor": "#172b4d", "activeTaskBkgColor": "#fff0bb", "activeTaskBorderColor": "#ba8a20", "critBkgColor": "#ffe5e5", "critBorderColor": "#bd5656", "doneTaskBkgColor": "#e4edff", "doneTaskBorderColor": "#3b6bb5", "sectionBkgColor": "#f7f9fc", "sectionBkgColor2": "#eff7f2", "sectionBkgColor3": "#f7f9fc", "taskTextDarkColor": "#172b4d", "taskTextOutsideColor": "#172b4d", "gridColor": "#d8e0e9"}}}%% gantt title Move preparation and KV loading into A's model-call window dateFormat YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss axisFormat %S tickInterval 10second todayMarker off section Native / Scheduler Prep A : a0, 2026-01-01T00:00:00, 5s CPU model call A : done, a1, 2026-01-01T00:00:05, 20s Retire C / prepare B : a2, 2026-01-01T00:00:25, 12s CPU call B : done, a3, 2026-01-01T00:00:40, 10s section Native / GPU A forward window : active, a4, 2026-01-01T00:00:07, 21s Exposed boundary : crit, a5, 2026-01-01T00:00:28, 14s B forward : active, a6, 2026-01-01T00:00:42, 8s section Native / B KV Load B : a7, 2026-01-01T00:00:32, 12s section V2 / Scheduler Prep A : b0, 2026-01-01T00:00:00, 5s Retire C : b1, 2026-01-01T00:00:06, 6s Receive : b2, 2026-01-01T00:00:12, 7s Prepare B : b3, 2026-01-01T00:00:19, 6s Handoff : b4, 2026-01-01T00:00:25, 5s section V2 / Forward worker CPU model call A : done, b5, 2026-01-01T00:00:05, 20s CPU call B : done, b6, 2026-01-01T00:00:30, 10s section V2 / GPU A forward window : active, b7, 2026-01-01T00:00:07, 21s Gap : crit, b8, 2026-01-01T00:00:28, 4s B forward : active, b9, 2026-01-01T00:00:32, 8s section V2 / B KV Early load B : b10, 2026-01-01T00:00:21, 12s ``` *Horizontal positions are schematic, in arbitrary units. Blue = CPU model call, green = scheduler work / KV loading, yellow = GPU forward window, red = exposed batch boundary. The bars do not represent measured durations or continuous GPU activity. B consumes KV as its required layers become ready, so its forward can overlap the loading tail.* Agent requests can also arrive while A's model call is running. V2 advances bounded, rank-consistent receive and preparation work during that window. A future turn that still depends on Decode completion must wait for that dependency. ## Modifications ### 1. Keep one scheduler-state owner The scheduler remains the only writer of requests, radix state, allocation, admission, and retirement. The forward worker executes the current model call and submits GPU work; existing backend paths perform KV loading. - **A:** the current prefill batch. - **B:** the next batch, prepared early when independent of A. - **C:** a previous batch whose independent result handling and PD completion can advance during A. **One state owner, separate execution and loading paths** ```mermaid %%{init: {"theme": "base", "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": true, "curve": "linear", "nodeSpacing": 35, "rankSpacing": 55}, "themeVariables": {"fontFamily": "Arial, sans-serif", "fontSize": "15px", "lineColor": "#7a8699", "edgeLabelBackground": "#ffffff", "clusterBkg": "#f7f9fc", "clusterBorder": "#d8e0e9"}, "fontFamily": "Arial, sans-serif"}}%% flowchart LR accTitle: One scheduler owner, separate forward and KV loading paths S["Scheduler owner
Retire C and prepare B
Only writer of shared state"] F["Forward worker
A model call
Kernel submission"] L["KV backend
HiCache / Mooncake
Load B's cached KV"] subgraph GPU["GPU"] A["A forward
Compute + communication"] B["B cached KV
Per-layer readiness"] end S -->|Run A| F S -->|Load B| L F -->|Kernels| A L -->|Transfer| B classDef owner fill:#dff2e8,stroke:#318463,stroke-width:2px,color:#172b4d classDef worker fill:#e4edff,stroke:#3b6bb5,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d classDef load fill:#eee5ff,stroke:#8159ba,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d classDef compute fill:#fff0bb,stroke:#ba8a20,stroke-width:1px,color:#172b4d class S owner class F worker class L,B load class A compute style GPU fill:#f7f9fc,stroke:#d8e0e9,stroke-width:1px,color:#596579 ``` ### 2. Advance independent work while A is being submitted At bounded, rank-consistent checkpoints, the scheduler can retire C, receive fresh independent requests, advance bootstrap, and prepare B. Target submission completion ends this preparation window; EAGLE Draft waits for preparation to finish before using shared TP/MoE state. These checkpoints bound eligibility and repeated progress, not the duration of each Python operation. Current V2 advances work during A's CPU model call; it does not restrict that work to explicit GPU-feedback waits. Evaluation therefore includes any extra A submission time rather than treating early work as free overlap. Each batch retains its own loading dependency snapshot. Preparing or loading B does not replace A's active dependencies. CUDA device/stream and relevant execution contexts are explicitly established in the forward worker. ### 3. Prepare a full B when safe; otherwise warm eligible KV | Situation | Early work | | --- | --- | | B is independent of A | Match prefixes, allocate, form B, and start its cached-KV load. | | B advances A's active chunk request | Warm eligible waiting requests' KV; retain shared-request advancement and final grouping at the normal boundary. | | A future agent turn has not been produced | Preserve the session dependency; it cannot be scheduled before it exists. | Speculative KV warming uses a shared page-aligned budget across candidates and outstanding transfers, while reserving compute headroom. The prototype scans up to eight candidates and uses an experimental 2M-token envelope for a 16K compute chunk. This is a tuning choice to validate, not an upstream default commitment. Normal admitted demand loads remain complete. ### 4. Use each backend's loading and lifetime rules | Backend | Loading path and ownership | | --- | --- | | HiCache | Background direct DMA; supported demand tails can use a bounded 16-CTA kernel, with direct fallback. Preserve current layout leases, address translation, allocator move protection, and completion events. | | Mooncake direct linker | Fully prepare an independent B using request-private load slots and a frozen per-batch dependency. Retain slots through its forward and publish through normal successful result handling. Preserve load failures and MLA dedup broadcasts. Chunk-follower KV-only warming is not enabled for this backend. | Cancelled or stale reservations retain transfer ownership until the associated writes have stopped. Request cancellation does not permit early page reuse. ### 5. Provide one opt-in switch Proposed switch: `--enable-overlap-schedule-v2`, default off. Existing settings select HiCache or the external linker backend. The switch is not implemented in upstream main yet. Initial compatibility targets are text-only CUDA PD prefill, PP1/DCP1, no independent DP request replicas, disabled CUDA graphs, and the CP8 DSA layer-split/EAGLE reference deployment. HiCache support here is host-L2 cache mode without a storage tier or buffer pipeline; HiCache L2 plus Mooncake L3 is not enabled. The direct linker bypasses the local host tier. Other combinations require explicit follow-up validation. The disabled path must preserve native scheduling, pause, shutdown, and chunk behavior. ## Accuracy Tests Local CPU protocol/profiler regressions and targeted real-PD cold/restored/mixed nonce checks have passed. These are not a comprehensive model-accuracy evaluation. Merge validation must retain and extend coverage of: - Registered owner/worker and cache-lifetime regression tests, including cancellation, delayed loads, failures, shared readers, reset, and shutdown. - GPU copy checks for nonidentity pages, untouched guards, and target/indexer/packed MTP layer mapping. - Model-output/logprob and task-appropriate accuracy checks against matched flag-off controls. - Consistent rank decisions and target/Draft handoff in the supported configurations. HTTP success, fixed output length, and byte-copy checks alone do not establish model accuracy. ## Speed Tests and Profiling These are **local main-port results against base 92580581da**, not results from the published empty diff. Each run uses GLM-5.3 FP8 with a separate 8×H200 Prefill node and 8×H200 Decode node. Native overlap remains enabled in both flags. Each pair is grouped by backend, HTTP concurrency, and repetition, with **OFF above ON**. **Bold identifies the better performance value within that pair**; cache hit and new-input counts are workload controls. Changes are `(ON / OFF − 1) × 100%`, approximately calculated from the displayed values: higher throughput is better; lower TTFT is better. ### HiCache host L2 — concurrency 20 | Pair | V2 | Input tokens/s ↑ | TTFT P50 ↓ | TTFT P99 ↓ | Total token cache hit | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | OFF | 194,454 | 4.397 s | 20.213 s | 88.834% | | 1 | ON | **204,389** | **3.978 s** | **19.768 s** | 88.834% | | 1 | ON vs OFF | **+5.11%** | **−9.53%** | **−2.20%** | — | | 2 | OFF | 193,790 | 4.437 s | **19.627 s** | 88.849% | | 2 | ON | **203,438** | **3.881 s** | 22.316 s | 88.834% | | 2 | ON vs OFF | **+4.98%** | **−12.53%** | +13.70% (worse) | — | ### Mooncake direct linker — concurrency 20 | Pair | V2 | Input tokens/s ↑ | TTFT P50 ↓ | TTFT P99 ↓ | Total token cache hit | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | OFF | 161,631 | 5.823 s | **20.246 s** | 88.834% | | 1 | ON | **172,085** | **5.183 s** | 22.724 s | 88.834% | | 1 | ON vs OFF | **+6.47%** | **−10.99%** | +12.24% (worse) | — | | 2 | OFF | 162,031 | 5.761 s | **21.715 s** | 88.834% | | 2 | ON | **171,888** | **5.165 s** | 23.548 s | 88.834% | | 2 | ON vs OFF | **+6.08%** | **−10.35%** | +8.44% (worse) | — | HiCache's two-run mean throughput increased **5.04%**, and the mean of run-level median TTFTs fell **11.04%**; mean run-level P99 increased 5.63%. Mooncake changed **+6.28%**, **−10.67%**, and +10.27%, respectively. These are means of run metrics, not pooled percentiles or a statistical guarantee. Tables are regrouped for comparison, not chronological: the order was OFF1 → ON1 → intervening experiments → ON2 → OFF2; a separate diagnostic run also preceded Mooncake OFF2. **Tail latency is not consistently improved.** Additional pairs change only the global HTTP budget to 10; active roots remain 20 and actual warmup/formal payload sets match concurrency 20: ### HiCache host L2 — concurrency 10 | Pair | V2 | Input tokens/s ↑ | TTFT P50 ↓ | TTFT P99 ↓ | New input tokens | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | OFF | 184,821 | 2.179 s | 12.585 s | 5,895,331 | | 1 | ON | **194,906** | **1.996 s** | **11.102 s** | 5,895,395 | | 1 | ON vs OFF | **+5.46%** | **−8.40%** | **−11.78%** | — | ### Mooncake direct linker — concurrency 10 | Pair | V2 | Input tokens/s ↑ | TTFT P50 ↓ | TTFT P99 ↓ | New input tokens | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | OFF | 157,597 | 2.726 s | 14.025 s | 5,895,395 | | 1 | ON | **166,313** | **2.562 s** | **13.581 s** | 5,895,331 | | 1 | ON vs OFF | **+5.53%** | **−6.02%** | **−3.17%** | — | The concurrency-10 pairs improve all three displayed performance metrics. Their improved P99 direction does not generalize to concurrency 20. ### Test configuration GLM-5.3 FP8; separate **8×H200 Prefill** and **8×H200 Decode** nodes. Selected flags from our test setup are shown below; these are configuration excerpts, not full reproduction commands. **Prefill — common to both cache backends** ```bash --disaggregation-mode prefill --tp-size 8 --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --enable-dsa-cache-layer-split --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --prefill-max-requests 8 --max-running-requests 64 --max-total-tokens 524288 --page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled ``` **Cache backend — choose one** ```bash # HiCache host L2: about 256 GiB of host-cache payload --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-host-memory-mode cache --hicache-ratio 3.5465017306928446 --hicache-mem-layout layer_first --hicache-io-backend direct --hicache-write-policy write_through # Or Mooncake direct linker: 32 GiB per P rank, about 256 GiB total --enable-unified-cache-external-linker --unified-cache-external-linker-backend mooncake # Storage config: protocol=rdma, global_segment_size=32gb per rank; # master address and device names are deployment-specific. ``` **Decode — unchanged between OFF and ON** ```bash --disaggregation-mode decode --tp-size 8 --attn-dp-size 8 --enable-dp-lm-head --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --enable-hisparse --hisparse-config '{"top_k":2048,"device_buffer_size":12288,"host_to_device_ratio":8}' ``` **OFF / ON:** native Prefill overlap remains enabled in both. ON adds `--enable-overlap-schedule-v2` to P; OFF omits it. HiCache ON also uses the bounded demand-transfer policy, so its result measures the combined feature. **Workload:** - Public Weka 256K traces: **80 root sessions**, seed `20261016`; **21 historical warmup requests**, then **903 formal requests**, all completed without errors. - Same formal payloads: **52,867,171 input tokens** and **16 output tokens/request**. Closed-loop HTTP concurrency **20 or 10**; session/subagent dependencies are preserved and slots release after the full response. - Same configured L1 and backing-cache capacities; total token cache hit is about **88.83%**. Formal prompts are not replayed for warmup; actual grouping and small cache-replacement differences can vary. **Draft status:** the results support the proposed overlap direction. Detailed trace analysis, final reproduction commands, and broader validation will be added once the implementation is finalized. Mooncake here uses P-host cache segments; cross-host cache scaling and HiCache L2 + Mooncake L3 are outside this measurement. ## Design and implementation plan - [RFC Issue #44721](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/44721) 1. Finalize and review the local owner/worker and backend implementation while preserving main's lifecycle protections. 2. Complete numerical/model and failure/cancellation coverage, and investigate tail-latency regressions. 3. Publish the verified runtime patch and reproduction commands; extend measurements to other supported deployments. ## Checklist - [x] Describe the design and ownership contract in the RFC and PR bodies, with inline diagrams. - [x] Report repeated local main-port OFF/ON tables, separate profiles, and observed regressions. - [ ] Publish and review the locally integrated runtime changes on main. - [ ] Add and run registered regression and GPU accuracy tests. - [ ] Publish reproducible main-based OFF/ON benchmarks and profiles. - [ ] Complete formatting checks, relevant CI, and review before implementation merge. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #38878199380](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38878199380) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #38878199398](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38878199398) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :heavy_minus_sign: **No AMD PR run found for this commit**.

items.title: [HiCache] Add KVCR as an L3 storage backend for hint-driven cross-instance KV reuse
items.body:
Implements [RFC #32903](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32903). Router-side companion: [ai-dynamo/dynamo#13591](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13591) (this PR is independently mergeable — without it the hint is simply never populated and the backend runs as a local-only L3 tier).

## Motivation

SGLang's existing HiCache L3 backends (mooncake, hf3fs, eic, …) all reach cross-instance reuse the same way: put KV in a *shared external store* every worker can address by content hash. That works well when such a store exists, but it is a deployment prerequisite, and it writes every offloaded page whether or not anyone will read it.

This PR adds a differently-shaped backend: **peer-to-peer, pull-on-demand, steered by the router**. KVCR (`nvidia-kvcr`, a framework-neutral KV cache runner with its own DRAM tier and a NIXL data path) already holds each worker's offloaded pages locally. The missing piece is knowing *which peer* holds a given prefix — SGLang cannot know that, and a destination worker cannot probe a peer's residency without a round trip per page. A KV-aware router already knows, because it builds a global prefix index from the `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` events SGLang publishes. So this PR makes that hint reachable from the storage backend, and adds the backend that acts on it. KV then moves only when the router has established that a specific peer holds a specific prefix a specific request needs — no shared store, no extra service, no speculative writes.

Two-worker loopback, dense Qwen3-8B, `--page-size 64`, once the distinct working set exceeds the device pool: **+53–59% qps, −50% TTFT**. An FP8 MoE model on the same harness: **+20%** — the dense number should not be extrapolated. Both predate the `kvcc`→`kvcr` rename. No cost when the backend is off: the hint is `None` on every path that does not set it, and the event change adds trailing nulls to a msgpack array.

## Modifications

One self-contained new backend (**+2287**), a thin per-request hint seam through existing code (**+308 / −30** across 14 files), and tests (**+2848**). Nothing outside the backend changes behaviour unless `--hicache-storage-backend kvcr` is selected.

**1. New backend — `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/kvcr/`.** `kvcr_store.py` (the whole `HiCacheStorage` surface: deposit/get, remote-hint path, per-rank control endpoints, counters), `router_hint.py` (the dynamo wire seam — normalizing block hashes between the router's `u64` and SGLang's page-hash prefix), `pin_adapter.py`, `kvcr_config.py`, and a reviewer's `README.md` covering how to run it, what was verified, and every known gap. Registered in `backend_factory.py`; v2 zero-copy path only.

**2. A per-request KV router hint, threaded end to end.** `GenerateReqInput.kv_router_hint` → `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` → `Req` → `Scheduler.prefetch` → `StorageOperation.router_hint` → `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info` → `batch_exists_v2`/`batch_get_v2`. An opaque `Optional[dict]` passed through untouched; the generic controller stays backend-agnostic by stashing it under a literal key in the free-form `extra_info` dict already threaded into every v2 call, and a test pins that literal against the backend's matching constant (a rename on one side is otherwise invisible — every hint just stops being found). Reviewer note: SGLang has **two** prefetch controller stacks (`HiCacheController` and `HybridCacheController`); both had to be threaded or the untouched one raises `TypeError`. Both host-memory modes (`cache` and `buffer_only`) work, and cost nothing extra, because the hint rides the *operation* rather than the host tier.

**3. KV event layout aligned with what routers parse positionally — and a live bug fix.** `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved`/`AllBlocksCleared` gain the trailing slots a cross-framework KV router expects at fixed positions (`lora_name`, `extra_keys`, then `group_idx`, `kv_cache_spec_kind`, `kv_cache_spec_sliding_window`, `locality`, `ownership`). SGLang populates almost none of them but must hold their places: these structs serialize as arrays, so a field appended into a slot the router reads as something else is silently *misinterpreted* rather than rejected. That is exactly what `cache_salt` was doing — it sat directly after `medium`, which is the router's `lora_name: Option<String>` slot, and a map landing there fails to decode and takes down **the entire published batch**, so one salted request could blind the router to every event beside it. The salt now goes in the positional `extra_keys` slot (prefix-tagged to match dynamo's `DYNAMO_CACHE_SALT_PREFIX`, pinned by a test) while the typed `BlockStoredWithMetadata` field stays parked past every position the router interprets. `KVCacheEventRecorder.enqueue` coalescing now compares the new fields, since it rewrites the tail's block-hash list in place.

**4. Guards for the rank layouts this backend cannot address.** A KVCR block key is `sha256(token ids)#<segment>` — it names the tokens and nothing about which slice of the model produced the bytes. `_rank_port_offset` separates `(dp, attn_cp, attn_tp)` by giving each rank its own control port; two coordinates have no such separation and both fail *open*, returning wrong KV with no error anywhere. `pp_size > 1`: `pp_rank` is not in the port offset, so `pp0/tp0` and `pp1/tp0` derive the same port and a hint aimed at one stage reaches the other. `should_split_heads`: head splitting exists so peers at different TP degrees can share a prefix, but this backend emits one key per page either way, so those peers agree on a key while holding different head slices. Both now raise at construction. Keyed on `should_split_heads` rather than `tp_lcm_size` deliberately — the controller accepts `tp_lcm_size` everywhere but resolves it to `False` for rank-replicated (MLA) models and non-`page_head` layouts, where the pooled key is correct; a test pins that distinction. Relatedly, and following the existing mooncake precedent, `kvcr` joins the set of backends for which **HiCache draft L3 is disabled**: on the generic draft path its v1 stubs would report a successful write then return `None` for every read, while a target-KV prefetch still admits the node, so load-back would copy stale bytes into draft host pages (output stays correct since proposals are verified, but acceptance silently degrades).

**5. Diagnostics for three silent HiCache failure modes.** All upstream behaviour, not backend-specific, but each presents as "the L3 backend is broken" and none logs anything today. Warnings only, no behaviour change. *Offload stalled* (`hiradix_cache.py`): `_update_host_leaf_status` admits a node to `evictable_host_leaves` only after the device tier drops it, so if the device pool is larger than the host pool, the host pool fills first, GPU eviction never fires, and L2+L3 both stop **for the life of the process** — it does not recover as entries age out. *Leaked prefetch reservation* (`cache_controller.py`): `prefetch_tokens_occupied` is reserved at creation and released only on the completion path, so a prefetch ending elsewhere leaks it permanently; once past the cap, L3 stops silently and `query_storage_hit_length` keeps reporting hits no `batch_get` follows. Rate-limited and leaked look identical from outside, so the counter is now logged. *`flush_cache` refused* (`scheduler.py`): the existing warning reports only request counts, so an in-flight HiCache op yields "0 queued, 0 running, still refused"; it now also reports write-through / load-back / prefetch / backup depths.

**6. `batch_get_v1`/`batch_set_v1` raise instead of returning `None`.** The non-abstract default was `pass`, but callers index the result or wrap it in `all(...)`, so an unimplemented backend surfaced as a `TypeError` **on the prefetch daemon thread, which HiCache never restarts** — silently disabling L3 for the process lifetime. Now `NotImplementedError`. Included because it is what makes the draft-L3 guard above honest; happy to split out.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel or model-forward changes. The real correctness risk here is different — a remote fetch returning the *wrong* KV would produce plausible, wrong output with nothing logged — so testing targeted that. **Under failure**, a remote fetch must degrade to recompute and never admit wrong KV: source frozen (`SIGSTOP`), source dead, and source restarted each matched the source-cached control arm word for word, 4/4, with the expected key present; no bad KV entered the radix tree in any run. **TP=2** bring-up found and fixed two silent per-rank bugs (a bind collision, and both ranks dialing the same source port) whose symptom was correct-*looking* output built from the wrong shard, so the test compares generated text rather than token counts. Methodology note that mattered: the control arm has to be *B-hinted vs A-cached*, not *A-fresh vs B-hinted* — the latter forks on sampling and produces false failures on its own.

Unit tests live in `test/registered/` and are all CPU-tier (`register_cpu_ci`, suite `base-a-test-cpu`) — no GPU and no `nvidia-kvcr` wheel required, since the KVCR-dependent cases skip cleanly when the wheel is absent. New: `test_kvcr_router_hint_schema.py` (the dynamo wire seam — `page hash → event i64 → router u64 → page key` round trip, malformed-payload fail-closed, the two-literal key agreement), `test_kvcr_router_hint_e2e.py` (hint path against the real KVCR core), `test_kvcr_tp_and_concurrency.py` (per-rank endpoints, concurrency, sidecar pools, the parallelism guards), `test_kvcr_config_validation.py`, `test_hicache_offload_stall.py`, `test_hicache_storage_thread_survival.py` (a raising backend must not kill the storage thread). Amended: `test_kv_events.py` (the full positional wire layout, pinned slot by slot) and `test_radix_cache_unit.py` (coalescing must not merge across the new fields). 87 passing in-container against `nvidia-kvcr` `873391c`. The parallelism guards were verified pre-fix: with the guard removed both rejection cases fail with `RuntimeError not raised`, while both acceptance cases stay green (they guard the opposite direction — over-rejection).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

See Motivation for the headline A/B. Capacity/sizing was swept separately across 4 configurations, one variable at a time, 95–130 distinct prefixes each.

## Known gaps

Listed up front rather than left to be found; all are in the backend README too. (1) **Host pool must be ≥ device pool** or offload stops permanently — upstream HiRadixCache behaviour; this PR adds the warning, not a fix. (2) **The default prefetch timeout silently discards a successful remote fetch.** `1.0 + 0.25 × tokens/1024` is under the measured remote-fetch latency (1.2–3.9 s for 31 pages), and losing the race throws the fetch away *after* every page has arrived: `increment` is refused on a terminated op, `completed_tokens` stays 0, nothing warns. Worked around with `prefetch_timeout_base: 15.0`, but **the right fix is probably upstream** — a backend-declared default, or not discarding a transfer that completed between the termination decision and the increment. Direction welcome. (3) **A peer restart costs ~34 s of degraded P2P** — KVCR-side, reported separately; transient, self-healing, no wrong answers. (4) **`local_dram_bytes` ≥ 32 GiB fails to start** — NIXL registration exceeds KVCR's 10 s progress-thread join timeout; KVCR-side. (5) **The source offers no framework memory as a NIXL source** — `pin_adapter.py` declines every pin, since safely pinning a HiCache host page needs a residency index inside HiRadixCache this backend does not have; everything served comes from KVCR's own tier, so the cost is a miss, never a wrong result. (6) **No DeepSeek / GLM-class model support, failing closed** — those models keep indexer/SWA/full-KV in separate pools with separate index spaces while KVCR's `framework_dram` registers a single region with one global slot size; the fix is a KVCR core API change (`framework_dram` → a list of `(region, slot_size)` declarations registered per class, essentially what mooncake already does with its multi-suffix keys). (7) **No model/tenant key namespace** — mooncake folds `model_name` and a backend tag into its key prefix; this backend does not. Fails closed today because each worker's tier is private, but it is the right next hardening step. (8) **`clear()` and `get_stats()` not implemented** — `flush_cache` logs success and clears nothing, and storage metrics come back empty. Both fail closed; `get_stats()` is cheap and could land here if reviewers want it.

## Questions for reviewers

Sections 3, 5 and 6 are independent of the backend and fix pre-existing issues — split into a separate PR, or keep them here where the motivation is visible? And on known gap 2, the prefetch-timeout discard looks worth fixing properly upstream rather than working around in config; preference on which direction?

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

items.title: feat(agent sessions): attribute stored KV cache blocks to sessions
items.body:
<!-- codex-pr-description:start -->
This PR adds optional request `session_id` metadata to SGLang `BlockStored` KV events while preserving the existing seven-element base wire payload when no metadata is present. It gives external KV routers enough engine-side evidence to associate stored block lineage with the triggering session without treating shared radix-cache blocks as session-owned.

### How This Was Implemented

- Extend `BlockStoredMetadata` with an optional `session_id` and include metadata in the wire payload only when at least one field is populated.
- Thread `Req.session_id` through finished and unfinished unified-cache inserts and request-driven unevict events.
- Keep `session_id` compatible with `cache_salt`; event metadata does not participate in block hashing or cache identity.
- Cover wire compatibility, metadata-aware coalescing, quiet shared-prefix hits, divergent-tail attribution, cache salt, and unevict behavior.

<details>
<summary>Walkthrough</summary>

#### Mental model

The event identifies the request that caused a physical store transition. It is not an owner list for a content-addressed block that several sessions may share.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Req.session_id"] --> B["InsertParams"]
    B --> C["UnifiedTreeCore insert or unevict"]
    C --> D["KVCacheEventRecorder"]
    D --> E["BlockStored metadata"]
    E --> F["External KV event consumer"]
```

#### Request lifecycle

The request's session identifier follows the same insertion context as the token IDs and optional cache salt. New pages and request-driven unevicts attach that identifier to `BlockStored`; a resident shared-prefix hit emits no duplicate store event, while a divergent tail links back to the shared parent hash and carries the session that created the tail.

#### Boundaries and limitations

Background HiCache transitions without request context remain unattributed, `BlockRemoved` remains unchanged, and events with different metadata do not coalesce. This change does not add vLLM-style opt-in full cache-hit reporting or change session-radix-cache ownership and lifecycle tracking.

</details>

### Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py::TestBlockStoredWireFormat test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py::TestKVCacheEventQueue test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py -k 'TestBlockStoredWireFormat or TestKVCacheEventQueue or session_id_is_attributed or session_id_and_cache_salt or shared_prefix_hit_is_quiet_and_divergent_tails_are_attributed'` — 11 passed, 2436 deselected.
- `uvx --from 'black==26.1.0' black test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` and `uvx --from 'ruff==0.15.1' ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037 test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py` — passed.
- Complementary Dynamo `SessionPrefixIndexer` regression combines two route-time shared-prefix matches with two session-attributed divergent tails — all 18 session-prefix-index tests passed.
- Live SGLang + Dynamo sidecar smoke test with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`: raw ZMQ emitted four stored block hashes with `session_id: session-e2e-001`; replay reported `#cached-token: 64` and Dynamo reported `overlap_blocks=4`; the request completed with HTTP 200.

Related Dynamo work: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13806 and https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13807

## Wire encoding change (added after review)

KV events are now **tagged msgpack maps**, not positional arrays. `KVCacheEvent` drops `array_like=True` and keeps `tag=True, omit_defaults=True`, so each event is `{"type": "<ClassName>", "<field>": ...}` and optional fields left at `None` are omitted. `cache_salt` and `session_id` are plain optional fields on `BlockStored`. `BlockStoredMetadata` and `BlockStoredWithMetadata` are removed. `EventBatch` stays a positional array `[ts, events, attn_dp_rank]`.

Why: positional arrays cannot grow. msgspec does not trim a trailing `None` in `array_like` structs (tested on 0.21.1), so salt metadata had to ride as an extra trailing element (#30827). That element landed in the `lora_name` slot of consumers that share a decoder with vLLM, and Dynamo dropped every salted batch (ai-dynamo/dynamo#14530 has the reproduction). Exported typed consumers could not read the salt either (#38561). vLLM moved its KV events to this exact map encoding in v0.24, so consumers now decode both engines with one code path.

This is a wire-format change for positional consumers. It will be called out in the release notes of the next SGLang release. The in-repo consumers (`experimental/sgl-router` and `sgl-kv-indexer`) decode the map shape only; the old array shape is rejected.

Size: a 16-token, 8-block `BlockStored` grows from about 666 to 755 bytes (keys); block hashes and token ids still dominate.

### Validation of the encoding change

- `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py`: events encode as tagged maps, unset optionals are omitted, one `KVEventBatch` decoder reads a mixed stream (unsalted, salted, session-attributed, removed, cleared), batch stays an array.
- `test_radix_cache_unit.py`, `test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`, `test_rust_tree_core_integration.py` updated to the plain fields and run on GPU.
- `sgl-router` wire decoder: 27 tests including msgspec golden bytes of a mixed map batch; `sgl-kv-indexer` bridge: 42 tests including map-form report/revoke/clear, ignored attribution keys, component-aware maps, and skipped undecodable maps.
- Dynamo main decodes the exact bytes this branch produces (cache namespace from `cache_salt`; `session_id` read once ai-dynamo/dynamo#13806 lands).

items.title: [Feature] Add process-local in-memory KV indexer and Router integration
items.body:
## Motivation

This PR supersedes #32662 with a smaller, dependency-free milestone for the KV
Indexer proposed in #31458.

The Indexer is an experimental metadata-only service that tracks which SGLang
worker may reuse each content-addressed KV-cache block. KV data remains owned by
the workers. The end-to-end path is:

```text
SGLang worker
  └─ ZMQ component-aware KV events
       └─ kv-indexer-bridge
            └─ gRPC
                 └─ process-local in-memory indexer
                      └─ MatchExternalKvPrefix
                           └─ experimental sgl-router
```

This revision removes Redis, Dragonfly, and Redis Cluster from the architecture.
Placement metadata is held in one Indexer process and is intentionally soft
state. That makes the core event → index → prefix-query path smaller, easier to
run, and directly testable without an external database.

Related:

- RFC: #31458
- Previous KV Indexer PR: #32662
- KV-event correctness fixes: #32537, #32514

## Scope and failure model

The process-local backend is protected by an `RwLock` and bounded request work.
It supports concurrent reads and serialized placement mutations in one server
process. It is not a distributed or persistent store.

- Run exactly one Indexer process for a deployment.
- Restarting the Indexer loses all placement metadata.
- There is no missed-event replay, restart fencing, worker liveness TTL, or
  cross-process replication in this milestone.
- A disconnected Bridge reconnects transport but cannot recover events emitted
  while it was absent. A batch the Indexer sheds, or refuses as oversized, costs
  those events and a reconnect rather than terminating the Bridge.
- A prefix hit only improves worker choice, so the Router degrades rather than
  failing when the Indexer cannot answer. An empty result, a rejection from
  either admission bound, a query that exceeds its deadline, and an unreachable
  Indexer all become no signal: the Router selects by minimum active load and
  logs at `WARN`. An Indexer outage therefore costs cache affinity rather than
  availability. Only a rejected RPC — the Router and the Indexer disagreeing on
  the request contract — still fails the request with `503`, because degrading
  would hide that disagreement from every request. An endpoint the Router could
  never dial is rejected at startup instead of failing every later query. The
  Router's local radix tree is used only when no Indexer endpoint is configured.

These constraints are explicit. This PR establishes a validated single-process
soft-state baseline; persistence and recovery belong in follow-up work.

## What changed

### Process-local memory backend

- Replace the Redis backend with an in-process component-aware placement map.
- Track `(block hash, worker, tier)` placement snapshots and worker cache specs.
- Support FULL, SWA, and MAMBA reusable-prefix semantics.
- Bound prefix scanning and request hash counts to keep work predictable.
- Remove Redis features, scripts, configuration, and integration requirements.

### Admission and resource protection

- Bound concurrent prefix queries in the Indexer.
- Shed queries whose caller deadline has already expired before backend work.
- Bound concurrent external Indexer queries in the Router.
- Add configurable Router timeout and max-inflight controls.
- Rate-limit rejection logs with doubling cadence to avoid log storms.

### Experimental Router integration

```bash
sgl-router \
  --model-id <model> \
  --tokenizer-path <tokenizer> \
  --worker-urls <worker URLs...> \
  --policy cache_aware_zmq \
  --kv-indexer-endpoint http://<indexer>:50061 \
  --kv-indexer-query-timeout-ms 100 \
  --kv-indexer-query-max-inflight 32
```

For each eligible request, the Router hashes normalized request tokens into the
same ordered block chain, calls `MatchExternalKvPrefix`, intersects returned
addresses with current routing candidates, and selects among the best reusable
prefix holders using active load.

### Component-aware prefix matching

The bridge accepts the gated `component_types` field from SGLang KV events and
stores a component snapshot for each placement. A versioned `WorkerCacheSpec`
describes which components and tiers are reusable.

- **FULL** must be present contiguously on every matched block.
- **SWA** must cover the configured trailing window at the candidate boundary,
  or form an unbroken run from the prompt head.
- **MAMBA** must be present on the candidate boundary block.

Component-aware placements without a valid worker cache spec fail closed.
Legacy whole-block events continue to use contiguous-prefix matching.

### Crate layout

`sgl-kv-indexer` lives inside the Router workspace, at
`experimental/sgl-router/sgl-kv-indexer`, as a workspace member. Both crates
share one lockfile, one toolchain, and one CI workflow. Membership also means
Cargo unifies features across the workspace, so the Indexer pins the same narrow
`zeromq` feature set as the Router (`tokio-runtime`, `tcp-transport`): adding it
neither enlarges the Router binary nor widens its license surface.

## Validation

### Current process-local backend: two machines, 15 Workers

One host runs a single Indexer (`prefix_query_max_inflight=32`) and the
experimental Router (`--policy cache_aware_zmq`,
`--kv-indexer-query-timeout-ms 100`). Two further hosts run 8 + 7 GPUs, giving 15
independent Workers each with its own Bridge, page size 64. Both component
profiles were driven end to end: FULL+SWA (`gpt-oss-20b-bf16`) and FULL+MAMBA
(`Qwen3.5-27B-FP8`). This is a Worker-density claim, not a host-count claim.

#### Placement and prefix correctness

| check | FULL+SWA | FULL+MAMBA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| expected blocks == Unified Tree cached blocks == Indexer prefix result | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| unique prefix routed by the Router to its exact holder | 15/15 | 15/15 |
| shared prefix routed to a holder from the shared set | pass | pass |

Prefix sizes differ per Worker by construction (SWA 104–118 blocks, MAMBA 13–41).
FULL+SWA routing was verified before and after churn.

#### Event replay against indexed state

The raw ZMQ event stream from both hosts (`BlockStored` / `BlockRemoved` /
`AllBlocksCleared`, including `component_types`) was replayed independently and
compared with the Indexer's `MatchExternalKv` snapshot, hash by hash and mask by
mask.

| scenario | stored events | removals | AllBlocksCleared | distinct blocks | Workers exactly equal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FULL+SWA, seed and selective flush | 3,135 | 0 | 24 | 1,665 | 15/15 |
| FULL+SWA, after 15 min churn | 101,475 | 2,353 | 54 | 28,416 | 15/15 |
| FULL+MAMBA, seed | 405 | 0 | 15 | 405 | 15/15 |
| FULL+MAMBA, after 5 min churn | 268,603 | 4,286 | 54 | 97,511 | 15/15 |

The churn rows cover eviction: caches were driven past capacity, so blocks were
removed and later re-stored. The MAMBA seed row also matched the expected mask
distribution, exactly one FULL|MAMBA checkpoint block per sequence and FULL only
elsewhere.

#### Cache churn

Concurrent generation, prefix reuse and capacity-exceeding requests across all 15
Workers, starting from a fresh `AllBlocksCleared` so both sides share one origin.

| profile | duration | requests | fresh / reuse / evicting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FULL+SWA | 15 min, 30 threads | 815 | 387 / 246 / 182 |
| FULL+MAMBA | 5 min, 15 threads | 3,984 | 1,626 / 1,380 / 978 |

Workers run `max_running_requests=1`, so the SWA churn saturated them and 111
client calls hit their read timeout; correctness is judged from the event stream,
not from client success.

#### Selective flush

Flushing one Worker, then all 8 Workers of one host: flushed placements dropped
to zero, untouched Workers kept their exact block counts, and the replayed event
state still equalled the Indexer state for 15/15 Workers. Verified for both
profiles.

#### MAMBA checkpoint boundary

Four probes per Worker, 15/15 passing: a query ending on the checkpoint block
returns the full prefix with the correct sole holder; including the trailing
partial page returns the same; one block short of the checkpoint returns 0; the
first block alone returns 0. Sweeping all truncation points for a 17-block
prefix, cuts 1–16 return 0 and cuts 17–18 return 17.

#### Query capacity and admission

Capacity was measured against the Indexer alone, with no GPUs: 15 synthetic
Workers holding 118-block FULL+SWA prefix chains, loaded through 15 real Bridge
processes, then queried by an increasing number of independent client processes
(16 threads each, co-located, 224-core host). Sweeping the process count is what
separates a driver limit from the server's: queries from a single Python process
are capped by its own interpreter, so one process cannot measure this server.

| client processes | in-flight callers | accepted qps | p50 ms | p99 ms | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 16 | 1,554 | 7.6 | 41.9 | 0 |
| 2 | 32 | 3,441 | 6.8 | 38.5 | 0 |
| 4 | 64 | 7,559 | 5.6 | 37.6 | 0 |
| 8 | 128 | 19,422 | 4.5 | 28.7 | 0 |
| 16 | 256 | 83,347 | 2.8 | 7.7 | 0 |
| 32 | 512 | 158,810 | 3.0 | 8.2 | 0 |
| 48 | 768 | 217,604 | 3.2 | 9.1 | 12 |
| 64 | 1,024 | 241,816 | 3.8 | 11.4 | 350 |
| 96 | 1,536 | 244,557 | 4.8 | 17.7 | 609,498 |

The original string-encoding run served roughly 245k prefix queries per
second at 118 blocks. Latency falls as clients are added rather than rising, up
to saturation, confirming that the low-process rows measure the driver.

The query-size sweep was re-run after changing hashes from decimal `string` to
packed `sfixed64`. This is a direct-parent A/B: commit `8e5fcd4054` versus
`39b5bdeaaa`, both release builds, with the same 15 Workers x 1,024-block state,
15-second stages, and the original saturation process count for each size.

| blocks per query | approx tokens | client processes | string qps | packed qps | change | p99 ms (string -> packed) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 64 | 128 | 429,141 | 369,186 | -14.0% | 14.2 -> 16.6 |
| 8 | 512 | 96 | 396,532 | 364,880 | -8.0% | 10.3 -> 13.2 |
| 32 | 2,048 | 128 | 362,378 | 355,003 | -2.0% | 14.1 -> 15.4 |
| 118 | 7,552 | 64 | 243,462 | 301,617 | +23.9% | 10.9 -> 9.0 |
| 256 | 16,384 | 64 | 182,357 | 267,709 | +46.8% | 14.4 -> 10.1 |
| 512 | 32,768 | 64 | 121,948 | 218,857 | +79.5% | 21.5 -> 12.2 |
| 1,024 | 65,536 | 64 | 74,310 | 143,859 | +93.6% | 37.4 -> 16.0 |

A least-squares fit of per-request cost gives 2.54 us fixed + 10.79 ns/block for
strings and 2.70 us fixed + 4.06 ns/block for packed hashes: the
length-dependent cost falls 62.4%. Short-query throughput is 2-14% lower; this
commit also adds a 64-stream per-connection bound, so the gRPC A/B does not
isolate encoding from that transport admission change at extreme concurrency.
Long-prefix throughput and latency improve substantially.

The in-memory state footprint improves too. With identical state (15 Workers x
16,384 unique FULL+SWA blocks, 245,760 blocks total), loaded-minus-idle PSS falls
from 120.6 MiB to 90.2 MiB (-25.2%) and RSS from 121.1 MiB to 90.8 MiB (-25.1%).
The first and last Worker's full 16,384-block matches were verified after load.

In the earlier string-encoding run, a query missing its first hash beat a fully
matching query by 6.8% at 118 blocks and 13.5% at 1,024. That showed tree scan
depth was only 6-12% of the old per-block cost; moving and decoding the hash
list dominated, which is consistent with the packed-encoding improvement.

**The inflight bound rejects as designed.** With
`prefix_query_max_inflight=32`, rejections begin at ~768 concurrent callers and
grow from there. At 1,536 callers the excess is shed while accepted throughput
holds near 245k qps and p99 stays at 17.7 ms, so the bound caps the tail instead
of letting queueing delay grow without limit.

**Deadline shedding is demonstrated.** 5,119 of 5,120 requests carrying a 1 ms
deadline were shed as `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` before backend work; one completed
before expiry. Shedding protects the Indexer, not the caller: like an admission
rejection, a shed query reaches the Router as no signal, so the request is still
routed, by minimum active load.

**Concurrent event ingestion is free at realistic event rates.** In the original
string-encoding run, 15 Bridges applying ~150 event batches/s returned 249,491
qps against a 248,681 qps idle baseline at 118 blocks, so applies and prefix
queries did not contend measurably.

Taken together: at the tested load points, the current packed implementation
serves 144k-369k queries/s across 1-1,024 blocks and does not reject below ~700
concurrent in-flight queries. Neither protection is expected to engage at
realistic Router query rates; both bound the tail, not the normal path.

**Router under Worker saturation.** With every Worker at capacity during churn,
16 concurrent end-to-end chat requests all exceeded the 30 s client timeout. The
Indexer saw zero errors in the same window and routing returned to 15/15 once
churn stopped, so this is Worker saturation rather than Router or Indexer
behaviour.

This is the scale claim for the process-local backend in this PR. A current
4/8-machine memory-backend result is intentionally not claimed.

### Event-pipeline evidence from the previous Redis-backed build

Before the backend replacement, the same component-event schema, Bridge decode
path, Unified Tree semantics, and prefix rules were validated at larger scale:

| deployment | phase | workers | Tree = Indexer = expected | raw event replay = indexed state |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 machines | FULL+MAMBA | 32 | 32/32 | 32/32 |
| 4 machines | FULL+SWA | 32 | 32/32 | 32/32 |
| 8 machines | FULL+MAMBA | 63 | 63/63 | 63/63 |
| 8 machines | FULL+SWA | 62 | 62/62 | 62/62 |

The 4-machine run also completed 15 minutes of churn with 4,224 checkpointed
Tree/Indexer alignment checks and zero failures. These results support event
production, Bridge decoding, component replacement, and holder attribution at
scale; they are not presented as 4/8-machine validation of the new memory
backend.

### Code and build gates

- One workspace gate over both crates: format, Clippy with warnings denied,
  release build, and **659 release tests** (107 Indexer, 552 Router), plus the
  tokenizer parity test run separately.
- `cargo deny` clean for advisories, bans, licenses, and sources.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed.
- Both Router images built from the final source: the release image's distroless
  entrypoint passed a `--help` smoke test, and the k8s e2e image runs
  `sgl-router` with its tokenizer fixture in place.

## Test coverage

The branch includes:

- memory-backend placement, tier, clear, and component-transition tests;
- FULL, SWA, MAMBA, and legacy prefix-rule tests;
- deadline, request-size, and max-inflight admission tests;
- gRPC validation, wire-contract, and client endpoint-validation tests;
- Bridge decoding and component-snapshot coverage;
- Router policy, fallback, degradation, configuration, and concurrency tests;
- process-local memory integration tests.

## Current limitations

- **Component metadata depends on #32514, which is not yet merged.** The
  `component_types` field on `BlockStored` and the
  `--enable-kv-events-component-types` option come from that PR.
- Metadata is process-local soft state and is lost on restart.
- Exactly one Indexer process is supported per deployment.
- No replay/reconciliation, liveness filtering, persistence, failover, or
  network-partition recovery is claimed. Bridge reconnect restores transport
  only; events missed while a Bridge was absent are not recovered, and this was
  not exercised.
- `KV_INDEXER_WORKER_ADDRESS` must match the Router worker URL byte-for-byte.
- Prefix scans are capped at 2,048 blocks (~131k tokens). A longer request is
  truncated rather than rejected, so it is matched on its first 2,048 blocks
  only.
- Worker density was validated at 15 Workers against one Indexer; higher
  densities only on the previous Redis-backed build.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and lint code according to repository conventions.
- [x] Add unit, contract, integration, and Router tests.
- [x] Update architecture, configuration, and limitation documentation.
- [x] Validate the final process-local backend on two machines.
- [x] Build and smoke-test the final Router Docker image.
- [ ] Confirm the updated PR CI is green.

items.title: [KV Cache] Align additive KV event metadata with shared consumers
items.body:
## Motivation

Shared KV-event consumers reject SGLang `BlockStored` messages because the required nullable `lora_name` field is missing. Consumers that derive salted cache keys from `extra_keys` also cannot find SGLang's salt there.

This draft contains an implementation of **proposed Phase 1 of #39991**. Replay framing and LoRA adapter-name/hash propagation remain separate follow-ups, so this PR does not close the RFC.

## Modifications

- Always serialize nullable `medium` and `lora_name`; producers emit `lora_name=None`.
- Emit the cache salt in `extra_keys` only for block zero of a full prefix. Keep entries aligned with `block_hashes` when stores coalesce, including padding absent entries. Preserve the named `cache_salt` and `session_id` fields.
- Apply the same metadata rule to the Rust adapter using its existing parent hash, block count, and salt. No Rust binding tuple or native implementation change is needed.
- Document the wire metadata and add registered CPU regression tests for required nulls, legacy decoders, coalescing, prefix continuations, and Python/Rust parity after extension and node splitting.

A separate commit relocates the unchanged MXFP8 reserved-slot test added by #35351 from `test/registered/kernel/quantization/` to `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/`. The latest upstream commit otherwise fails the repository's registered-test taxonomy check; the failure was reproduced on unmodified `main`. This is a path-only correction with no test-content changes.

Block hashes, storage-tier names, batch layout, and transport framing are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output changes. Validation used local Linux ARM64 CPU execution with the real compiled Rust extension, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0, and msgspec 0.21.1:

```bash
python -m pytest --noconftest \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core_integration.py \
  -k 'not test_memory_allocated' -q -rs -p no:cacheprovider
```

Result: **173 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected; 89 subtests passed**. The skipped test requires CUDA. The existing `test_memory_allocated` is deselected because it calls `torch.get_device_module().memory_allocated()`, which is unavailable on CPU.

The CPU suite, changed-line coverage, and full pre-commit checks were rerun after rebasing onto `main` at `0cb37c018c`. All passed after the path-only test relocation described above.

Additional checks:

- The same suite passed with `--cov --cov-config=.coveragerc --cov-report=xml`. `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch=origin/main --fail-under=60` reported **100% of changed executable lines covered (13/13)**.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed with the repository's Rust toolchains.
- `mint@4.2.559 validate` and `mint@4.2.559 broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` passed.
- `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-speed claim. This changes opt-in event metadata and does not modify model execution, kernels, or scheduling. No GPU inference benchmark was run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered regression tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide relevant validation; model accuracy and GPU speed benchmarks are not applicable to this metadata change.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

This PR is on hold as a draft pending maintainer agreement on #39991, following the [issue author's clarification](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39991#issuecomment-5779276096). The implementation and validation results are preserved for reference. Further implementation updates and CI requests are paused until the RFC scope is agreed.
